results.title: Platelet Activation by Antisense Oligonucleotides (ASOs) in the Göttingen Minipig, including an Evaluation of Glycoprotein VI (GPVI) and Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) Ontogeny
results.authors_year: Jordal, Berridge, et al. (2023)
results.species_and_system: Göttingen minipig platelet-rich plasma and whole blood in vitro (activation assay + aggregometry), explicitly cross-tabulated against published human PRP/whole-blood and NHP data for the same seven constructs
results.why_relevant: The single highest-value record found. Table 1 gives complete per-position chemistry for 7 tool ASOs — PS linkage positions marked residue-by-residue with asterisks, 2'MOE sugar positions as uppercase, LNA positions as underlined uppercase — with length and explicit PS load (e.g. ODN2395 22-mer/21 PS; ISIS104838 2'MOE/PS/2'MOE gapmer 20-mer/19 PS; RTR5001 LNA/PS/LNA 14-mer/13 PS), plus isosequential PO and all-PS variants that isolate backbone from sugar chemistry. Table 2 is a purpose-built human/NHP/minipig bridge matrix for those same 7 constructs across in vivo and in vitro platelet endpoints. Mechanism is PS ASO binding to platelet collagen receptor GPVI, stated to mirror human blood findings. CC BY, so tables are directly reusable.

results.title: A Comparative Study of Porcine and Ovine Derived Defibrotide: Coagulation Profiles, Molecular Characteristics, and DNA Content
results.authors_year: Clin Appl Thromb Hemost (2026)
results.species_and_system: Human blood-bank pooled plasma plus individually analysed healthy volunteer donor plasma and citrated human whole blood, spiked at 100 µg/mL
results.why_relevant: Closes gaps 1 and 4 simultaneously and is the only record found that does so. 19 porcine and 9 ovine defibrotide API batches each assayed by aPTT and thrombin time in human plasma and whole blood, with anti-Xa and anti-IIa amidolytic activities — directly the anti-Xa and contact/common-pathway endpoint set requested. Characterisation is per-batch: DNA content by heparin-red quantification and molecular weight distribution by size-exclusion HPLC (tandem PSK 2000/3000, heparin fraction calibrators 2,000–50,000). Methods state donor plasma was analysed individually and not pooled, so donor-level conditions are recoverable. Caveat the authors disclose: no untreated control samples were included.

results.title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex
results.authors_year: Sheehan & Lan, Blood (1998)
results.species_and_system: Human plasma in vitro coagulation assays plus purified human component systems (thrombin clotting activity, heparin cofactor II)
results.why_relevant: Foundational human in vitro record for the PS-backbone coagulopathy signal. ISIS 2302 (20-mer PS, anti-ICAM-1) characterised in human plasma and in purified human enzyme systems, locating the dominant effect at the intrinsic tenase (FIXa-FVIIIa) complex, with prothrombin-time and thrombin-time prolongation above ~100 µg/mL and a separate heparin-cofactor-II-mediated component. The abstract itself frames the work as explaining clotting-time prolongation seen in both monkey and human dosing of the same construct, so it anchors a same-construct bridge with PMID 9316823 (human volunteers) and PMID 9361909 (cynomolgus).

results.title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex by an allosteric mechanism
results.authors_year: Biochemistry (2001)
results.species_and_system: Purified human coagulation factors (FIXa, FVIIIa, FX, phospholipid) and human plasma aPTT
results.why_relevant: The quantitative mechanistic follow-up to the record above, and the best purified-human-factor dataset found. States plainly that PS oligodeoxynucleotides prolong aPTT in human plasma by inhibiting intrinsic tenase activity, then dissects it with ISIS 2302: hyperbolic mixed-type inhibition of FX activation, Vmax(app) decomposition across complex assembly, cofactor stability and protease catalysis, with controls showing no inhibition of FIXa-phospholipid FX activation and no significant effect on FVIII-phospholipid affinity. Gives mechanism-level parameters rather than a single clotting-time shift, which is what distinguishes a reusable in vitro assay row from an observation.

results.title: Effects of synthetic oligonucleotides on human complement and coagulation
results.authors_year: Biochem Pharmacol (1997)
results.species_and_system: Normal human donor plasma and human blood in vitro; hemolytic complement assay
results.why_relevant: Explicitly constructed as the human in vitro counterpart to the unanticipated monkey findings, which is exactly the bridge framing gap 2 asks for. PS-oligo inhibited normal human blood clotting with concentration-dependent prolongation of clotting times including aPTT, measured alongside prothrombin fragment F1+2 and hemolytic complement in the same donor plasma — giving a coagulation and complement readout on one material, useful for separating contact-pathway activation from complement-driven effects in the dataset.

results.title: Effects of phosphorothioate oligodeoxyribonucleotide and oligoribonucleotides on human complement and coagulation
results.authors_year: Bioorg Med Chem Lett (1998)
results.species_and_system: Human plasma in vitro aPTT and complement lysis
results.why_relevant: The only record found that resolves the aPTT effect by sugar chemistry class within one experiment: synthesised and compared PS-oligodeoxyribonucleotide (DNA) against PS-oligoribonucleotide, 2'-O-methyl-RNA and 2'-5'-RNA analogues for aPTT prolongation and complement lysis inhibition in vitro, concluding PS-DNA prolongs aPTT and inhibits complement lysis more than the PS-RNA analogues. That is a chemistry-resolved structure-activity axis for coagulopathy, directly serving the Phase 2 requirement to locate chemical modifications rather than just name a compound.

results.title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety of fesomersen, a novel antisense inhibitor of factor XI, in healthy Chinese, Japanese, and Caucasian volunteers
results.authors_year: Clin Transl Sci (2024)
results.species_and_system: Healthy human volunteers (three clinical studies, three ethnic groups), subcutaneous dosing, FXI activity and clotting-time PD
results.why_relevant: Open-access (CC BY-NC) human PK/PD/safety dataset for a GalNAc-conjugated FXI ASO across three ethnic cohorts, which lets FXI-lowering and the resulting clotting-time change be read against exposure rather than dose alone. Three studies reported in one paper, so it is efficient to ingest, and the ethnic-cohort structure supports covariate work that single-cohort trial reports cannot. Full text is retrievable, so PD tables and any sequence/chemistry statement are inspectable without a paywall route.

results.title: Factor XI antisense oligonucleotide for prevention of venous thrombosis
results.authors_year: Büller et al., N Engl J Med (2015)
results.species_and_system: 300 human patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty, randomised open-label FXI-ASO (ISIS 416858) vs enoxaparin
results.why_relevant: The pivotal human interventional dataset for a second-generation 2'-MOE PS antisense agent whose on-target effect is itself a coagulopathy: FXI level reduction with corresponding aPTT prolongation, read against adjudicated VTE and bleeding endpoints in 300 participants. Free full text is available as a PMC author manuscript, so the endpoint tables are reachable without a subscription. Pairs with PMID 22246038 below on the identical construct.

results.title: Antisense inhibition of coagulation factor XI prolongs APTT without increased bleeding risk in cynomolgus monkeys
results.authors_year: Younis et al., Blood (2012)
results.species_and_system: Cynomolgus monkey, up to 13 weeks subcutaneous dosing; liver FXI mRNA, plasma FXI activity, APTT, bleeding models
results.why_relevant: Supplies the animal half of a genuine same-construct human-to-animal bridge: ISIS 416858 is the identical 2'-MOE antisense inhibitor of FXI dosed in the NEJM trial above. Reports a dose-dependent FXI reduction (liver mRNA and plasma activity) with concomitant APTT increase across 4–40 mg/kg/week, plus explicit bleeding-risk assessment at 20 and 40 mg/kg/week. Because both the exposure-response and the APTT endpoint are measured in the same units as the human study, the two can be aligned rather than merely compared qualitatively — which is the specific operation gap 2 requires.

results.title: Fitusiran prophylaxis in people with severe haemophilia A or haemophilia B without inhibitors (ATLAS-A/B): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
results.authors_year: Srivastava et al., Lancet Haematol (2023)
results.species_and_system: Human, 45 sites in 17 countries, males aged 12+ with severe haemophilia A or B without inhibitors, randomised 2:1 to 80 mg monthly subcutaneous fitusiran vs on-demand clotting factor concentrates, 9 months
results.why_relevant: This is named acquisition target 5 and I confirmed the exact primary publication: PubMed's NCT03417245 secondary-source index resolves to this record and no other trial report. Fitusiran is an antithrombin-targeting siRNA whose mechanism is deliberate induced hypercoagulability, so its safety appendix is the counterpart case to the aPTT-prolonging ASOs — the thrombotic-event and antithrombin-level data are the coagulopathy endpoint. Access caveat: no PMC record and not in Europe PMC, so the full text and safety appendix are behind Lancet Haematol; I found no legal open copy via PMC or EPMC.

results.title: First-in-human experience of an antidote-controlled anticoagulant using RNA aptamer technology: a phase 1a pharmacodynamic evaluation of a drug-antidote pair for the controlled regulation of factor IXa activity
results.authors_year: Dyke et al., Circulation (2006)
results.species_and_system: Healthy human volunteers, phase 1a; REG1 system (RB006 modified-RNA aptamer drug, RB007 complementary oligonucleotide antidote)
results.why_relevant: Covers the pegnivacogin/REG1 branch of the named vocabulary with first-in-human dose-response clotting-time data, and is mechanistically distinct from every other record here: anticoagulation is the intended pharmacology via FIXa binding, and it is actively reversible by a complementary oligonucleotide. That reversal arm is unusually informative for the dataset because it gives a within-subject on/off control on an oligonucleotide-driven clotting-time change. Pairs with PMID 18284597 (randomised repeat-dose PD study of the same pair) for a dose-ranging extension.

results.title: Pharmacokinetic properties of ISIS 2302, an antisense inhibitor of intercellular adhesion molecule-1, in healthy male volunteers (rising-dose, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial)
results.authors_year: Glover et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther (1997)
results.species_and_system: Healthy male human volunteers, single and multiple IV infusions, 0.06–2.00 mg/kg over 2 h
results.why_relevant: Completes a same-construct triangle that no other compound in this search offers: ISIS 2302 measured in human volunteers here, in human plasma and purified human factors in PMIDs 9716589 and 11305914, and in cynomolgus monkeys in PMID 9361909. Reports brief dose-related aPTT increases timed to Cmax with Cmax linearly related to dose, plus clinically insignificant C3a rises at higher repeated doses while C5a, blood pressure and pulse were unaffected — giving a concentration-anchored human in vivo aPTT point that can be regressed against the in vitro inhibition constants from the same molecule.

coverage_log.notes:
RESOURCE PERFORMANCE: PubMed via NCBI E-utilities (esearch.fcgi + efetch.fcgi, JSON and XML) worked without authentication, rate-limiting or CAPTCHA across 31 queries. No barrier for the resource itself. I used the API throughout and never scraped the web UI, per the hard rules.

ONE METHOD CORRECTION WORTH FLAGGING: my first efetch parser used an XPath of './/ArticleIdList/ArticleId', which also matches ArticleIdList elements nested inside each record's ReferenceList, so early output attached reference DOIs/PMCIDs to the wrong parent article (e.g. PMID 38563414 initially showed a spurious PMC7249474 and a Bioanalysis DOI). Fixed by anchoring to 'PubmedData/ArticleIdList'. Every identifier in the results above was re-verified against Europe PMC's core record, so the DOIs/PMCIDs reported are correct. If the parent agent is running similar parses on PubMed XML, this is a live trap.

ACCESS ROUTES ATTEMPTED, AND HOW TO READ THE 'access' VALUES: for each shortlisted record I queried Europe PMC core metadata for isOpenAccess/pmcid/inEPMC. Two records marked 'technical_block' (PMID 9716589 Blood 1998, PMID 22246038 Blood 2012) are not confirmed paywalls — Blood's archive is normally free after an embargo, but HEAD requests to ashpublications.org returned HTTP/2 403 through this environment's agent proxy, so I could not verify. These are worth one retry from a different route before anyone pays for them. Records marked 'abstract_only' have no PMC record and no Europe PMC full text; I did not find an author manuscript or repository copy for them. No purchases, subscriptions, credentials or author contact were used.

RANKING LOGIC: ordered by the Phase 2 criteria as instructed, not by row count. Gap 3 (sequence + per-position chemistry) and gap 4 (purity/characterisation) are the dataset's binding constraints, so the top two records are the two that actually carry that material — PMID 37111598 for position-level chemistry and PMID 41869748 for per-batch characterisation — ahead of much larger trials. Items 3–6 are the human in vitro mechanism core (gap 1). Items 7–11 are human dosed endpoints. Item 12 is ranked last among human studies only because its own value is modest; its worth is as the keystone of the ISIS 2302 bridge.

TWO STRUCTURAL FINDINGS BEYOND THE INDIVIDUAL RECORDS:
1. The ISIS 2302 cluster (PMIDs 9716589, 11305914, 9316823, plus 9361909 cynomolgus APTT with ex vivo spiking into untreated monkey blood, and 9184201 the 4-week monkey toxicity study) is the most complete single-construct human-in-vitro / human-in-vivo / animal chain in the indexed literature. If the dataset needs one worked bridge example to demonstrate the extrapolation the challenge asks about, this is it, and most of it is 1997–2001 so the chemistry is simple and fully described in-text.
2. The ISIS 416858 / FXI-ASO pair (PMID 25482425 human, PMID 22246038 cynomolgus) is the modern equivalent with a clinically dosed 2'-MOE gapmer, and the human half is free in PMC.

NAMED ACQUISITION TARGETS — STATUS AGAINST GAP 5:
- ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245: FOUND, primary publication confirmed as PMID 37003278 (Lancet Haematol 2023) via PubMed's [si] secondary-source index, which returned only two records for that NCT and one is a meeting abstract compilation. Paywalled, no open copy located. Sister trials also located if useful: ATLAS-INH PMID 37003287 (NCT03417102, Lancet 2023) and ATLAS-PPX PMID 38452197 (Blood 2024, PMC11181353, open access — the only openly accessible fitusiran phase 3 report found, so it is the cheapest route to fitusiran safety-table structure).
- Volanesorsen APPROACH (ISIS 304801-CS6) supplementary appendix: NOT FOUND as such. PubMed indexes the trial literature but not sponsor protocols or supplementary appendices; the appendix itself is a publisher-hosted artefact outside PubMed's scope. Recommend redirecting this target to ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (results + document section, which sometimes carries the protocol/SAP PDF) or the journal site, not to a bibliographic index.
- Mipomersen ISIS 301012-CS5 / CS7 (RADICHOL II) / CS12 individual safety tables: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. PubMed does not index by sponsor protocol code, so I resolved the trials by NCT instead and recovered the phase 3 set: NCT00794664 (PMID 23152839, PLoS One 2012, PMC3496741, OPEN ACCESS — severe hypercholesterolaemia, n=58), NCT00706849 (PMID 23060426, Circulation 2012 — HeFH + CAD), NCT00770146 (PMID 24013058, JACC 2013 — high CV risk, n=158), NCT00694109 (PMID 24366918, Eur Heart J, PMC4344956, OPEN ACCESS — 2-year open-label extension, n=141), and a pooled four-trial analysis PMID 25614280 (PMC4344404, OPEN ACCESS) covering NCT00607373/00706849/00770146/00794664 with n=382. Mapping these NCTs onto the CS5/CS7/CS12 protocol codes needs a sponsor-document source; PubMed cannot do it. The three open-access ones are the practical acquisition targets.

WHAT PUBMED STRUCTURALLY CANNOT CLOSE: gap 4 at scale. The purity/characterisation query returned 622 records, but these are analytical-method papers (ion-pair LC-MS, CE for oligonucleotide impurity profiling) that characterise generic or unrelated oligos, not the tested material of the coagulation studies in the dataset. Only PMID 41869748 tied per-batch characterisation to coagulation assays on that same material. Per-compound purity for clinically dosed oligos lives in regulatory review documents (FDA/EMA CMC sections) and sponsor CoAs, which are not indexed here. I did not pad the list with the analytical-method hits.

HONOURABLE MENTIONS NOT IN THE TOP 12, all verified: PMID 38537676 (Kidney Int 2024, fesomersen phase 2b in haemodialysis, dose-response 40/80/120 mg vs placebo with a major-bleeding composite primary safety endpoint — strong human endpoint record, no PMC); PMID 37042966 (Blood Adv 2023, PMC10546346, OPEN — HRG- and FXII-directed ASOs in rabbits with aPTT, PT and catheter-induced thrombin generation before/after treatment, >90% target knockdown; clean animal-side contact-pathway data); PMID 18284597 (JTH 2008, randomised repeat-dose PD study of the REG1 drug-antidote pair); PMID 22398951 (Thromb Haemost 2012, prekallikrein ASO in mice with aPTT, relevant to the donidalorsen prekallikrein branch); PMID 12438559 (JPET 2002, ISIS 104838 — note this is the same gapmer whose per-position chemistry appears in PMID 37111598 Table 1 and which causes thrombocytopenia in humans and NHPs, so it is a second ready-made bridge candidate with sequence in hand).

results.title: A Comparative Study of Porcine and Ovine Derived Defibrotide: Coagulation Profiles, Molecular Characteristics, and DNA Content
results.authors_year: Clin Appl Thromb Hemost, 2026
results.species_and_system: HUMAN. Citrated blood-bank plasma (Loyola University Medical Center Blood Bank) plus citrated whole blood from multiple healthy adult volunteers aged 18-40, processed and analysed individually, NOT pooled across donors. Verified by reading the OA full text, not the abstract (the abstract says only 'pooled plasma').
results.why_relevant: The single best dual-gap record found in this resource. Closes gap 1 and gap 4 simultaneously for an oligonucleotide drug. Human plasma and human whole blood spiked at 100 ug/mL with 28 separate API batches (19 porcine, 9 ovine) of defibrotide, read out by aPTT (Instrumentation Laboratory ACL 300), thrombin time (Stago ST4), and amidolytic anti-Xa and anti-IIa. Reported result is a NEGATIVE aPTT finding (no anticoagulant effect in aPTT for either source) with mild comparable effect in TT - a genuine human in vitro negative control point, which a coagulopathy dataset needs as much as positives. Separately provides batch-level tested-material characterisation: size-exclusion chromatography molecular weight (ovine 16.8 +/- 0.24 kDa vs porcine 18.02 +/- 0.32 kDa) and DNA content by heparin red method (75.78 vs 79 ug per 10 ug API). Caveat for dataset entry: defibrotide is a polydisperse DNA-derived polyelectrolyte, so there is no single definable sequence - record it as a mixture with MW distribution rather than forcing a sequence field. Also note the paper states untreated control samples were not included.

results.title: Sequence-specific 2'-O-methoxyethyl antisense oligonucleotides activate human platelets through glycoprotein VI, triggering formation of platelet-leukocyte aggregates
results.authors_year: Haematologica, 2022
results.species_and_system: HUMAN. Human cord-blood-derived megakaryocytes (proplatelet production) and whole blood from healthy human volunteers (surface P-selectin, platelet-leukocyte aggregates); GPVI binding affinity measured directly.
results.why_relevant: Highest-value gap 1 record for the phosphorothioate platelet/thrombocytopenia axis, and it is explicitly sequence-resolved, which is rare. Five named phosphorothioate ASOs tested side by side: three 2'MOE compounds - ISIS 487660 (no effect on platelet count), ISIS 104838 (associated with clinical phenotype 1 platelet decline), ISIS 501861 (effect unknown) - plus two CpG sequences, ISIS 120704 and ODN 2395. All five bound platelet GPVI with KD ~0.2-1.5 mM; CpG had highest affinity and greatest activation; 487660 showed no detectable platelet effect while 104838 and 501861 drove SYK-dependent platelet-leukocyte aggregate formation. Critically for the Phase 2 criteria, it reports donor-level stratification: donors with higher platelet GPVI levels showed greater ASO-induced activation, which is exactly the kind of human-system variance data the challenge asks for. None of the ASOs inhibited proplatelet production, which localises the mechanism to activation rather than production. Named compound IDs make per-position chemistry recoverable even where this paper does not print the base sequence.

results.title: The Influence of Plasma Prekallikrein Oligonucleotide Antisense Therapy on Coagulation and Fibrinolysis Assays: A Post-hoc Analysis
results.authors_year: Fijen, Petersen, Meijers, Bordone, Levi, Cohn; Thromb Haemost, 2022
results.species_and_system: HUMAN ex vivo. Patient plasma from a phase 2 randomised trial, 22 hereditary angioedema patients, donidalorsen 80 mg (IONIS-PKKRx, prekallikrein-targeted 2'MOE ASO) vs placebo, baseline and 4-month follow-up.
results.why_relevant: The most complete human coagulation panel found on a clinically dosed antisense oligonucleotide, and it is fully extractable: the Europe PMC record carries no abstract, so this is only visible by reading the CC-BY full text, which I did. Table 1 gives numeric baseline/follow-up/delta values with p-values and reference ranges for silica-based aPTT (reported as remaining within reference values), calibrated automated thrombogram lag time, peak thrombin and ETP, factor XI activity, prothrombin fragment 1+2, thrombin-antithrombin complexes, high-molecular-weight kininogen activity, normalised clot lysis time, D-dimer, plasminogen activity, and plasmin-alpha2-antiplasmin complexes. Median prekallikrein reduction 75% (range 36-94%). Directly addresses the contact-pathway question in gap 1 with a human-system readout, and because prekallikrein deficiency itself prolongs aPTT, the negative aPTT result here is a mechanistically load-bearing data point. Ionis co-authorship (Bordone) means these are sponsor-grade assay data.

results.title: Assessing single-stranded oligonucleotide drug-induced effects in vitro reveals key risk factors for thrombocytopenia
results.authors_year: Sewing et al.; PLoS One, 2017
results.species_and_system: HUMAN. Human platelets in vitro; human haematopoietic cell differentiation culture.
results.why_relevant: The structure-activity backbone for gap 1: it converts 'phosphorothioates activate platelets' into a quantitative chemistry relationship in a human system. Shows PS-oligonucleotide binding to human platelet GPVI and, newly, to platelet factor 4, with binding and subsequent human platelet activation correlating with oligonucleotide LENGTH and with the NUMBER OF PHOSPHOROTHIOATE LINKAGES in the backbone. Also shows locked nucleic acid (LNA) ribosyl modifications in the wings strongly suppress both GPVI and PF4 binding and markedly reduce platelet activation - i.e. per-position chemistry changes the coagulopathy readout, which is precisely the extrapolation axis the Phase 2 call privileges. Explicitly framed as a prospective in vitro assay battery for deprioritising thrombocytopenia-liable candidates, so the assay conditions are documented for reuse. PS count and length are both encodable as dataset covariates.

results.title: Phosphorothioate backbone modifications of nucleotide-based drugs are potent platelet activators
results.authors_year: Flierl et al.; J Exp Med, 2015
results.species_and_system: HUMAN platelets (plus animal work in the same paper).
results.why_relevant: The originating mechanistic paper attributing platelet activation specifically to the PHOSPHOROTHIOATE BACKBONE rather than to sequence or target, across nucleotide-based drug classes. It is the reference that the Haematologica and Sewing human-platelet studies build on, so including it gives the dataset the mechanistic root node for the whole PS-backbone coagulopathy cluster. Open access in PMC with no retrieval barrier. Because it spans human platelets and in vivo animal work within one paper, it is also a candidate partial bridge for gap 2, though the construct matching across species needs checking against the methods before claiming it as one.

results.title: RNA interference therapy targeting coagulation factor XI: a first-in-human trial of RBD4059 (vortosiran)
results.authors_year: Gabrielsen et al. (Ribocure/Suzhou Ribo); Blood Advances, 2026
results.species_and_system: HUMAN. Phase 1 single ascending dose, healthy volunteers, randomised 6+2 active:placebo across four subcutaneous cohorts 50-600 mg, followed to day 169.
results.why_relevant: HUMAN HALF OF THE CLEANEST HUMAN-TO-ANIMAL BRIDGE I FOUND. Same named construct (RBD4059, GalNAc-conjugated siRNA targeting FXI) measured here in humans and in mice and monkeys in the companion record below, so the two sides are directly comparable - which is exactly what gap 2 asks for and is usually impossible to assemble because sponsors publish preclinical and clinical data under different compound labels. Reports dose-dependent, durable suppression of FXI activity exceeding 90%, with safety and tolerability as primary endpoint to day 169, plus PK/PD modelling supporting 3-6 month dosing. FXI activity is the pharmacodynamic coagulation readout, so this is on-target coagulation modulation rather than off-target coagulopathy - worth encoding with that distinction explicit, since conflating intended FXI knockdown with phosphorothioate contact-pathway toxicity would corrupt the dataset.

results.title: Inhibition of Factor XI Using RBD4059: A Novel GalNAc-siRNA With Potent and Durable Antithrombotic Effects
results.authors_year: JACC Basic Transl Sci, 2025
results.species_and_system: ANIMAL. Mice and cynomolgus monkeys (FXI inhibition, duration), mouse thrombosis models, mouse tail bleeding model.
results.why_relevant: ANIMAL HALF OF THE RBD4059/VORTOSIRAN BRIDGE. Pair this with PMC13083634 above and the dataset gains a matched same-construct human/animal comparison for a GalNAc-siRNA acting on the coagulation cascade: potent durable FXI inhibition in both mice and monkeys, antithrombotic efficacy in mouse thrombosis models, and no prolonged bleeding in the mouse tail bleed assay, against >90% FXI suppression and no safety signal in human healthy volunteers. That lets the extrapolation the Phase 2 call asks for (animal to human system) be computed rather than asserted. Both halves are open access with no retrieval barrier.

results.title: Chemistry, structure and function of approved oligonucleotide therapeutics
results.authors_year: Egli & Manoharan; Nucleic Acids Research, 2023
results.species_and_system: Not applicable - chemistry reference work covering 18 approved nucleic acid therapeutics.
results.why_relevant: Best single instrument found in this resource for gap 3, where only 14 of 38 human-dosed compounds currently have a printed sequence and 11 have position-level chemistry. Systematic treatment of the chemistry of approved oligonucleotide therapeutics with per-modification structural detail across phosphorothioate, 2'-F-RNA, 2'-O-methyl RNA, 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl)-RNA (MOE) and phosphorodiamidate morpholino chemistries. Disease coverage explicitly includes homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (mipomersen), hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (inotersen) and familial chylomicronemia syndrome (volanesorsen) - the three approved compounds that carry the heaviest coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia signal in this dataset. Open access in PMC. Use it to populate position-level chemistry for approved compounds; it will NOT cover the discontinued or investigational ISIS-numbered compounds, which still need sponsor filings or patent literature.

results.title: Assessment of Platelet Aggregation and Thrombin Generation in Patients with Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome Treated with Volanesorsen: A Cross-Sectional Study
results.authors_year: Biomedicines, 2024
results.species_and_system: HUMAN ex vivo. 4 FCS patients on volanesorsen plus 4 matched healthy controls; samples processed by calibrated automated thrombogram (CAT, PPP-reagent LOW) and turbidimetric platelet aggregation against multiple agonists.
results.why_relevant: Rare functional human coagulation phenotyping on a clinically dosed ASO, as opposed to platelet counts alone. Gives numeric thrombin generation parameters for patients and controls (LagTime, ttPeak, StartTail, Velocity Index, ETP, peak thrombin - e.g. ETP 599.80 +/- 73.47 in patients vs 900.2 +/- 210.99 in controls) alongside platelet count change from baseline of 30% at week 12 and 34% at week 36. Finding is that thrombin generation and aggregation stayed within range with no significant case-control difference despite the platelet count drop, which is a mechanistically important dissociation: volanesorsen lowers platelet NUMBER without a detectable global haemostatic functional deficit. Must be entered with n=4 and the cross-sectional design on its face - it is a small-n study and its value is the assay depth and the dissociation finding, not statistical weight. Note Europe PMC also holds a preprint of the same work (10.20944/preprints202407.0557.v1); dedupe against the journal version.

results.title: The Effects of 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Containing Antisense Oligonucleotides on Platelets in Human Clinical Trials
results.authors_year: Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, 2017
results.species_and_system: HUMAN. Ionis integrated safety database (ISDB): over 2,600 human subjects across 16 different 2'MOE ASOs, placebo-controlled and open-label, doses to 624 mg/week, durations to 4.6 years.
results.why_relevant: The denominator record for the 2'MOE platelet signal, and it is sequence-discriminating at the class level, which matters for the dataset's extrapolation claims. Establishes there is no class-generic 2'MOE effect on platelet number, no confirmed counts below 50 K/uL, and only 7 of 2,638 subjects (0.3%) with a confirmed post-baseline count between 100 and 50 K/uL - but that 3 of 16 2'MOE ASOs had >10% incidence of platelet decreases >30% from baseline, i.e. the liability is sequence-specific rather than chemistry-generic. That conclusion is the clinical counterpart to the in vitro sequence-specificity in PMC8804562 and PMC5673186, so the three together let the dataset link a human in vitro assay result to a human trial outcome. Also reports no evidence of altered platelet FUNCTION, including from the factor XI ASO trials. Does not print sequences; compounds are referenced at class level.

results.identifier: PMID 31390500 / DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1715944 (APPROACH, volanesorsen, sponsor protocol ISIS 304801-CS6)
results.title: Volanesorsen and Triglyceride Levels in Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome
results.authors_year: Witztum et al.; N Engl J Med, 2019
results.species_and_system: HUMAN. APPROACH randomised placebo-controlled phase 3, 33 volanesorsen vs 33 placebo.
results.why_relevant: NAMED ACQUISITION TARGET FROM GAP 5, PARTIALLY CLOSED BY A LEGAL OPEN ROUTE. The NEJM version is subscription-only and has no PMC record, but Europe PMC's fullTextUrlList surfaced an author/institutional repository copy at Amsterdam UMC Pure flagged 'Open access'. I fetched it and confirmed HTTP 200, a real 414 KB PDF, and extracted the adverse event table from it: platelet count decreased 11/33 (33%) volanesorsen vs 1/33 (3%) placebo; petechiae 4 (12%) vs 0; epistaxis 5 (15%) vs 0; injection-site reaction 20 (61%) vs 0. These are directly enterable coagulopathy rows for a clinically dosed ASO. IMPORTANT LIMITATION, verified by text scan of the retrieved PDF: it contains the main article only. Zero matches for 'supplementary appendix', 'sequence', 'purity' or 'aPTT'. So the SUPPLEMENTARY APPENDIX half of this gap-5 target remains unclosed, and the per-patient platelet time course, sequence and purity data presumably in it are still outstanding. Try the FDA/EMA review documents or the sponsor protocol next, not Europe PMC.

results.identifier: PMID 9716589 / DOI 10.1182/blood.v92.5.1617 (with companion PMID 11305914, DOI 10.1021/bi002396x, Biochemistry 2001)
results.title: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex (1998); companion: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex by an allosteric mechanism (2001)
results.authors_year: Sheehan & Lan, Blood 1998; Sheehan & Phan, Biochemistry 2001
results.species_and_system: PURIFIED HUMAN COAGULATION FACTORS. Intrinsic tenase complex (factor VIIIa/factor IXa activation of factor X) in a reconstituted purified system.
results.why_relevant: The mechanistic anchor for phosphorothioate aPTT prolongation at the purified-human-factor level, which is the most reductionist tier of gap 1 and the tier the dataset most lacks. Together the pair establishes that PS oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex and do so by an ALLOSTERIC mechanism, not simple polyanionic surface sequestration - that distinction determines whether aPTT prolongation should be modelled as concentration-linear nonspecific polyanion effect or as a saturable binding event, and it changes how the dataset should extrapolate between assay formats. Found alongside two further foundational closed-access records from the same era: 'Inhibition of coagulation by a phosphorothioate oligonucleotide' (PMID 9361909, Antisense Nucleic Acid Drug Dev 1997) and Henry et al. 'Effects of phosphorothioate oligodeoxyribonucleotide and oligoribonucleotides on human complement and coagulation' (PMID 9873494, Bioorg Med Chem Lett 1998). ACCESS: Europe PMC advertises the Blood 1998 full text as 'Free after 12 months' at the legacy bloodjournal.org URL, but I followed the DOI and ashpublications.org returned HTTP 403 - see the barrier field. Abstract is free; full text was not retrievable by any open route from this resource.

coverage_log.barrier: The Europe PMC REST API itself was fully usable - no login wall, CAPTCHA, rate limit or API error at any point across 24 queries. The search endpoint, resultType=core retrieval and the fullTextXML endpoint all returned results, and I read OA full text for three records (PMC9718591, PMC13009829, PMC13083634-adjacent checks). Barriers were per-record retrieval blocks only, recorded exactly: (1) Sheehan & Lan, Blood 1998, PMID 9716589 - Europe PMC fullTextUrlList advertises 'Free after 12 months | html | http://www.bloodjournal.org/cgi/content/full/92/5/1617'; following https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.v92.5.1617 redirected to https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/92/5/1617/247353/Phosphorothioate-Oligonucleotides-Inhibit-the and returned HTTP 403. No PMC record, no author manuscript, no preprint. Abstract free only. (2) ATLAS-A/B primary publication, PMID 37003278, DOI 10.1016/S2352-3026(23)00037-6, Lancet Haematology 2023 - record found, but pmcid null, isOpenAccess N, inEPMC N, hasSuppl N, sole fullTextUrl availability 'Subscription required'. No open copy anywhere in Europe PMC. Same for the companion ATLAS-INH paper, PMID 37003287, DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(23)00284-2. The safety appendix is therefore NOT obtainable from this resource. (3) Henry et al. 1998, PMID 9873494 - 'Subscription required' only, no PMC, no repository copy. (4) Volanesorsen APPROACH, PMID 31390500 - NEJM version subscription-required, but a legal institutional-repository copy at Amsterdam UMC Pure was listed as Open access and fetched successfully (HTTP 200, 414393 bytes, application/pdf); its supplementary appendix is absent from that PDF. (5) NCT03417245 searched as a free-text term returned 50 records but none was the ATLAS-A/B primary report with its appendix. No tool was available to extract PDF text (pdftotext absent); I extracted the APPROACH PDF content via a Python zlib/regex stream decode instead, which is why the AE figures above are quoted rather than tabulated.
coverage_log.applicability: Highly applicable. Europe PMC is the single most productive bibliographic resource for gap 1, because its open-access full-text corpus plus CC-BY licensing means human coagulation assay tables can actually be read and extracted, not just cited - two of the strongest records here (the donidalorsen coagulation/fibrinolysis panel and the defibrotide human plasma batch study) were only assessable by reading full text, and one of them carries no abstract in the index at all. It is weak for gap 4: a dedicated purity/characterisation query crossing purity, HPLC-purified or endotoxin against phosphorothioate/ASO and platelet/coagulation/complement/thrombin returned exactly ONE irrelevant hit, confirming that purity and tested-material characterisation are essentially never reported in the abstracts of oligonucleotide coagulation studies; the large purity literature that does exist in this resource is generic analytical-method work on unrelated compounds (nusinersen generic comparability, siRNA impurity HILIC-MS) with no coagulation endpoint, so it cannot be used to characterise the material in the coagulation rows. Gap 4 will need CMC sections of regulatory filings, not the bibliographic literature. It is also structurally unable to close the gap-5 appendix targets, since those live in publisher-hosted supplementary files behind subscription (ATLAS-A/B) or in sponsor protocols that are not indexed here at all (mipomersen ISIS 301012-CS5, CS7/RADICHOL II, CS12 - no standalone records for these individual trials were retrievable by any of my queries).
coverage_log.notes:
RANKED BY PHASE 2 CRITERIA, NOT ROW VOLUME. Order above is deliberate: human in vitro/ex vivo systems first (1-5), matched human-animal bridge second (6-7), sequence/per-position chemistry third (8), human trial endpoints fourth (9-11), purified-human-factor mechanism last (12) only because of its access block, not its value.

TWO HUMAN-TO-ANIMAL BRIDGES, NOT ONE. The RBD4059/vortosiran pair (results 6 and 7) is the clean one - same named construct, human phase 1 and mouse/monkey, both open access. But there is a SECOND bridge worth assembling that I did not have a slot for: ISIS 104838 appears in the human system in result 2 (Haematologica, human volunteer blood and human cord-blood megakaryocytes, moderate platelet activation, SYK-dependent aggregates) AND in cynomolgus monkey in 'Investigation into the Mechanism(s) That Leads to Platelet Decreases in Cynomolgus Monkeys During Administration of ISIS 104838, a 2'-MOE-Modified Antisense Oligonucleotide' (PMID 29846725, Toxicol Sci 2018, DOI 10.1093/toxsci/kfy119, subscription required, no PMC). That is the same construct in both species with mechanism work on each side. If an open route to the Toxicol Sci paper can be found elsewhere, this becomes the highest-value bridge in the dataset, because unlike RBD4059 the endpoint is off-target platelet toxicity rather than intended target knockdown.

RUNNERS-UP, DROPPED ONLY FOR THE 12-SLOT CAP, all open access in PMC and all gap-1 relevant: (a) PMID 33540294 / PMC8264460, Thromb Res 2021, 'Antisense oligonucleotides and nucleic acids generate hypersensitive platelets' - one of only three hits on a tightly-scoped human-donor-plus-PS-chemistry-plus-coagulation abstract query, so it is a genuine human-system record. (b) PMID 23692437 / PMC3816843, J Thromb Haemost 2013, FXII-targeting RNA aptamer, dose-dependently prolongs fibrin clot formation and thrombin generation in clinical coagulation assays - oligonucleotide acting on the contact pathway in a human plasma system, and aptamer papers normally print full sequence. (c) PMID 28632925 / PMC5818257, J Thromb Haemost 2017, kallikrein-targeting RNA aptamer inhibiting the intrinsic pathway and reducing bradykinin release - same value profile. (d) PMID 38563414 / PMC10985948, Clin Transl Sci 2024, fesomersen (FXI ASO) PK/PD/safety across Caucasian, Japanese and Chinese healthy volunteers, three studies, dose-dependent FXI reduction - human trial endpoint with an ethnicity covariate. (e) PMID 37093125, Nucleic Acid Ther 2023, complement C3d/C4d deposition on platelets correlating with 2'MOE ASO thrombocytopenia in monkeys - the complement-platelet mechanism link, subscription only. (f) PMID 42381708 / PMC13315839, Mol Ther Nucleic Acids 2026, meta-analysis of adverse events across ASO clinical studies - useful as a cross-check on dataset completeness for human AE rows, though aggregate rather than primary.

ONE METHODOLOGICAL WARNING ABOUT THIS RESOURCE. Europe PMC relevance ranking is strongly recency-biased: broad unfielded queries on this topic returned almost entirely 2025-2026 narrative reviews and buried the primary mechanistic literature. Every high-value record above came from TITLE: or ABSTRACT: field-restricted queries or from an exact-title lookup. If this search is repeated or extended, use field restriction - a broad keyword sweep will systematically miss the 1997-2018 primary papers that carry the actual assay data.

DATASET-ENTRY CAUTIONS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) Distinguish on-target anticoagulation from off-target coagulopathy. Results 6, 7 and runner-up (d) are FXI/FXII-targeted agents where reduced clotting is the intended pharmacology; results 2, 4, 5 and 12 are phosphorothioate backbone toxicity. Encoding both as 'coagulopathy' without that flag would make the dataset's extrapolations meaningless. (2) Defibrotide (result 1) has no single sequence - it is a polydisperse DNA-derived polyelectrolyte characterised by a MW distribution, so the Phase 2 'sequence of all oligos tested' requirement cannot be satisfied for it and should be recorded as not-applicable-with-reason rather than left blank or forced. (3) Result 9 exists as both a journal article and a 2024 preprint in this index - dedupe. (4) Result 12's access status is honest: abstract free, full text blocked at HTTP 403, so any values taken from it must come from a route I did not have, not from this search.

results.title: Phosphorothioate backbone modifications of nucleotide-based drugs are potent platelet activators

Direct PS-backbone-dependent human platelet activation, signalling, ROS, adhesion, spreading, aggregation and in vitro thrombus formation, with GPVI identified as the receptor. The GPVI-deficient patient platelets give a human mechanistic negative control, and the paired mouse in vivo work makes it a bridge record as well. A single defined 20-mer PS ASO (ISIS 2302, anti-ICAM-1) titrated in human plasma with PT, thrombin time and aPTT endpoints, then dissected in purified human component assays. results.authors_year: Capaldi DC, Teasdale A, Henry SP, et al. 2017, Nucleic Acid Therapeutics 27(6):309

No OpenAlex API key is configured in this environment and I did not create one (hard rule: no credentials/sign-ups). coverage_log.applicability: Highly applicable as a discovery and open-access-routing layer: OpenAlex indexes the entire oligonucleotide coagulation literature and its per-work "locations" array is the single most useful field here, because it reveals legal green/bronze copies (PMC, Amsterdam UMC Pure, institutional repositories) for papers whose publisher version is paywalled. Its limitation for this endpoint is that it carries only titles, abstracts and metadata - it holds no sequence tables, no per-position chemistry, no purity certificates and no assay-level measurements, so it can locate and triage gap-3 and gap-4 evidence but can never itself close those gaps; the supplementary files must be pulled from the resolved full-text host.
coverage_log.notes:
RANKING BASIS: ordered by the Phase 2 criteria (human in vitro system first, then human/animal extrapolability, then sequence and per-position chemistry, then purity), not by row volume. Results 1-3 and 9 are human in vitro/ex vivo (gap 1); 4, 6, 7 are same-construct or same-class cross-species bridges (gap 2); 8 is the best sequence-and-modification panel (gap 3); 12 is the only purity reference found (gap 4); 5, 10, 11 are named acquisition targets (gap 5).

GAP-5 SCORECARD. (a) ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245 primary publication: LOCATED (W4361195612, DOI 10.1016/S2352-3026(23)00037-6, PMID 37003278) but NOT OBTAINED - closed at Lancet Haematol, and the only green deposit is 401-walled at Southampton. (b) Volanesorsen APPROACH (ISIS 304801-CS6): CLOSED via the Amsterdam UMC Pure green copy, result 11. coverage_log.notes:
WHAT THIS RESOURCE IS ACTUALLY GOOD FOR HERE. Keyword relevance search was poor: generic coagulation queries returned mostly off-target records (seaweed sulfated polysaccharides, FXIa small molecules, plasma freezing stability) because the ranker keys on the coagulation vocabulary and ignores the oligonucleotide constraint. The productive mode was the CITATION GRAPH. One call to /paper/DOI:10.1089/oli.1.1997.7.503/citations?limit=100 — forward citations of the 1997 phosphorothioate/coagulation paper — yielded four of the five human in vitro records in this list, including both Sheehan intrinsic-tenase papers that keyword search never surfaced. A second call on the FXI-ASO cynomolgus paper yielded the human/animal bridge pairs. RECOMMENDATION for the remaining 429-blocked ground: do not re-run keyword searches here; instead run /citations and /references on the seeds this sweep established (PMID 9716589, 11305914, 9873494, 25093529, 28145801), which costs one request per seed instead of one per query.

ON GAPS 3 AND 4. Nothing in this sweep closes them, and the resource structurally cannot. Semantic Scholar indexes titles, abstracts, identifiers and an openAccessPdf pointer; it does not index supplementary material, so the APPROACH supplementary appendix and the ATLAS-A/B safety appendix are invisible to it even where it finds the parent paper. The two open repository copies it did resolve (Southampton eprints 477603, Amsterdam UMC Pure 157436303) are author accepted manuscripts, and AAMs frequently omit supplementary files — treat the sequence/purity question as still open until those downloads are inspected. Route gaps 3 and 4 to PMC OA subset full text, journal supplementary endpoints, and regulatory documents (FDA/EMA assessment reports, which do carry drug substance characterisation and purity), not to bibliographic indexes.

TWO CAUTIONS ON THE LIST ABOVE. First, PMID 25093529 measures complement, not clotting; it earns its place as a same-construct human/monkey bridge calibration but must not be ingested as a coagulopathy measurement. Second, the Southampton open copy for ATLAS-A/B has a filename referring to ATLAS-INH (the inhibitor cohort, a different publication, PMID 37003287); verify arm identity on download before attributing it to NCT03417245 ATLAS-A/B.

ALREADY-IN-SOURCES CHECKING IS WEAK. I could only see one register file, and it carries structured PMIDs for roughly one record, so grep against it is not a reliable membership test. Only PMID 25482425 was positively confirmed present. Everything else is marked UNKNOWN rather than FALSE — do not read UNKNOWN as new. Two of the twelve (PMID 28145801, 31390500) also appear in a sibling agent's working candidate file in the shared scratchpad, which suggests parallel discovery and a possible dedupe step before ingestion.

ONE NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING. PMID 42486782 (2026), 'Assay-dependent Artifactual Prolongation of Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT) in Cynomolgus Monkeys: Potential Role of POEGMA', DOI 10.1177/10915818261470772, not open access. Animal-only so it did not make the twelve, but it argues that some reported oligonucleotide aPTT prolongation is an assay artifact rather than a biological effect. If that holds it bears on how aPTT rows across the whole dataset should be qualified, and it is worth a look independently of this gap list.

results.title: RNA Sequencing reveals transcriptome profiling of HUVECs in response to NETs +/- defibrotide
results.authors_year: 2021; GEO release 2021-10-13
results.species_and_system: Homo sapiens — primary human umbilical vein endothelial cells, 9 samples; vehicle vs neutrophil extracellular traps vs NETs + defibrotide
results.why_relevant: The closest GEO comes to a human oligonucleotide-plus-thrombosis record: defibrotide (on the dataset's named vocabulary) applied to human endothelial cells under a NET-driven prothrombotic stimulus, with 229 differentially expressed genes versus NETs alone. Logged as adjacent-but-not-qualifying.

results.title: Rescue of blood coagulation Factor VIII exon-16 mis-splicing by antisense oligonucleotides
results.species_and_system: Homo sapiens, 32 samples; in vitro transcribed F8 exon 16 RNA, SHAPE chemical probing with 2A3 vs DMSO (confirmed from series_matrix: molecule subtype IVT RNA, tissue N/A)
results.why_relevant: The only record in all of GEO returned by 'antisense oligonucleotide AND coagulation' and by 'antisense oligonucleotide AND coagulopathy'. Recorded for completeness of the negative result: it is an RNA-structure/splice-rescue efficacy study on naked in vitro transcribed F8 RNA aimed at treating haemophilia A, not an oligonucleotide-induced coagulopathy measurement, and it uses no human plasma, blood, platelets or purified factors. It should not be entered as a coagulation row.

coverage_log.notes: Verdict: GEO is a LOW-YIELD resource for this endpoint and should be closed out rather than re-searched. 45 queries executed against db=gds; zero coagulation-function measurements exist in the archive, and that is a property of the archive rather than of the queries — GEO stores expression matrices, and aPTT/PT/INR/thrombin generation/anti-Xa/TEG/ROTEM/anti-Xa values have nowhere to live in a GEO record. Gaps 1, 4 and 5 are unclosable here and no further GEO effort should be spent on them. Specifically on the gap-5 acquisition targets: NCT03417245 (ATLAS-A/B), the APPROACH appendix (ISIS 304801-CS6) and the mipomersen CS5/CS7/CS12 safety tables are trial documents and have no GEO representation; queries for mipomersen, fitusiran, volanesorsen (1 hit, a mouse apoC-III/apoE metabolism study, GSE131284), and eplontersen/olezarsen/donidalorsen/custirsen (0 hits) all came back empty or irrelevant. Searches for the contact pathway returned nothing usable: SERPINC1 siRNA 0, antithrombin siRNA 0, factor XII oligonucleotide 0, F11 antisense 4 hits all false positives (breast fibrosis, medulloblastoma, X-inactivation), kallikrein antisense 2 hits both false positives. One concrete follow-up is worth doing and is cheap: the GSE40261 finding shows GEO sample metadata sometimes contains the full sequence plus the per-position modification scheme, so a bulk fetch of the SOFT family files for the 304 'phosphorothioate' and 1,481 'gapmer' hits, grepped for 5'-...-3' strings and modification keywords, could mechanically harvest sequence/chemistry records for gap 3 at low cost via the FTP route (which is not CAPTCHA-protected). That is a sequence-annotation exercise for research-grade ASOs, though — it will not produce sequences for the 24 clinically dosed compounds still missing them, since those appear in GEO rarely if at all. Method note for reproducibility: use E-utilities and GEO FTP, not the acc.cgi web UI, which serves a reCAPTCHA challenge to non-browser clients.

results.authors_year: SRA/GEO submission, 2021
results.species_and_system: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC), in vitro, treated with neutrophil extracellular traps with and without defibrotide (20 ug/mL class, 4 h)

It does not close gap 1 because the readout is transcriptomic, with no aPTT, thrombin generation, platelet or contact-pathway measurement, no donor coagulation parameters, and defibrotide is a polydisperse porcine-derived mixture for which no single sequence or purity specification can be recorded.

coverage_log.notes: What the query hits actually are. Every coagulation-vocabulary query either returned zero or resolved to false positives from SRA's loose free-text matching across protocol fields: "aPTT" (29) = runs in study SRP280133 "IDENTA-1" with sample names like P3B_X; "ROTEM OR thromboelastography" (3883) = wheat DArTSeq (ERP133670) and a Nile crocodile genome, i.e. substring noise; "contact activation" (149) = K562/RPE1 nuclease-digestion controls; "factor XII" (12) = F12-knockout mouse diabetic-kidney study SRP483355 with no oligonucleotide; "oligonucleotide toxicity" (23) = a renal proximal-tubule cell-source comparison (SRP511301); "oligonucleotide AND plasma AND Homo sapiens" (1568) = AND-matching, not plasma coagulation work. Hard zeros that matter for the named acquisition targets: "volanesorsen OR inotersen OR mipomersen OR fitusiran OR olezarsen OR eplontersen OR donidalorsen" = 0 (NCBI explicitly reported all seven phrases not found), "IONIS" = 0, "ISIS 301012" = 0, "NCT03417245" = 0, "apolipoprotein C-III AND antisense" = 0, "factor XI AND antisense" = 0, "thrombin generation" = 0, "anti-Xa" = 0, "prekallikrein" = 0, "2'-MOE" = 0, "antisense oligonucleotide AND coagulation" = 0, "phosphorothioate AND coagulation" = 0, "gapmer AND coagulation" = 0, "oligonucleotide AND aPTT" = 0, "phosphorothioate AND platelet" = 0, "platelet AND siRNA" = 0, "megakaryocyte AND antisense" = 0, "antisense AND cynomolgus" = 0. No barrier: E-utilities answered every request without login, CAPTCHA or error; counts and ID lists were returned and individual records were retrieved with esummary and efetch. Separate constraint worth logging: several studies that match oligo-chemistry vocabulary are embargoed rather than blocked — SRP537023 (GSE279011, phosphorothioate-treated PC3), SRP723143 (GSE342032, 2'-O-methoxyethyl ASO387/ASO550 in SK-MEL-28, release 2027-08-11) and SRP709271 (GSE335367, release 2026-06-30) are listed as private with scheduled release dates, so their metadata cannot be read today. Recommendation: do not re-run SRA for gaps 1, 2, 4 or 5; the only defensible SRA deliverable is the ERP021077 sequence/LNA-count table, and even that is mouse-dosed research ASOs with no coagulation endpoint. For gap 3 on clinically dosed compounds, Europe PMC supplementary tables, patent literature and FDA/EMA review documents dominate this resource. Machine-readable parse of ERP021077 saved nothing to the repo; the 13 sequences and their LNA counts are listed in full in the result above so no file read is needed.

coverage_log.resource: PRIDE (PRoteomics IDEntifications Database, EMBL-EBI) — https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/ — searched via open REST API v3 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/ws/archive/v3/search/projects)
coverage_log.applicability: PRIDE is a mass-spectrometry proteomics data archive: its unit of deposit is raw/processed MS files plus protein identification tables, so it structurally cannot hold functional coagulation assay readouts (aPTT, PT/INR, thrombin generation, anti-Xa, TEG/ROTEM), platelet count or donor-level clinical safety data, and it does not archive oligonucleotide sequences, per-position chemistry or certificate-of-analysis purity data as curated fields. Exhaustive querying confirms the structural expectation: 1,116 unique project records were retrieved and screened, and zero deposits pair a therapeutic oligonucleotide with a coagulation or haemostasis endpoint. PRIDE closes none of the five gaps and should be logged as searched-and-not-applicable rather than retried.

results.title: Identification and functional validation of intracellular protein partners of phosphorothioate-splice switching oligonucleotides through AP-MS
results.authors_year: Strasbourg/Sorbonne consortium, 2026 (DOI 10.1016/J.OMTN.2026.102832; Mol Ther Nucleic Acids)
results.species_and_system: Human in vitro — differentiated human muscle cells (KM571 myoblast line, DMD exon 52 deletion); biotinylated SSO pulldown on streptavidin beads, nanoLC-MS/MS (timsTOF Pro)
results.why_relevant: The only PRIDE deposit that systematically compares phosphorothioate-backbone oligonucleotide protein binding ACROSS defined 2'-sugar chemistries (tricycloDNA vs LNA vs 2'-MOE) in a human cell system. Mechanistically adjacent to the gap-1 question of why PS backbones engage plasma contact-pathway proteins, and the chemistry arms are explicitly labelled. BUT: intracellular interactome only — no plasma, no whole blood, no platelets, no purified factors, and no coagulation readout of any kind. The oligo is a DMD exon-51 splice switcher, not a clinically dosed compound in our 38. Chemistry is specified at backbone/class level, not per position, and no purity or identity data accompany the deposit. Logged for completeness; it does not close a gap.

results.title: Inhibition of the RNA exosome by chemically stabilized long antisense oligonucleotides
results.authors_year: Franz-Wachtel / Stafforst lab, University of Tubingen, public 2026-09-30
results.species_and_system: Human in vitro — HeLa cells, triple-SILAC proximity biotinylation (SNAP-BASU), Q Exactive HF
results.why_relevant: Human in vitro demonstration that oligonucleotide protein binding is dependent on sequence, length and 2'-ribose modification — the same structure-activity logic that drives PS-backbone contact activation. Relevant only as mechanistic background for the chemistry axis of the dataset. No coagulation endpoint, no blood-derived matrix, no clinical compound, no purity characterisation, and no printed sequences in the archive metadata. Does not close a gap.

coverage_log.notes:
METHOD. Used the PRIDE open REST API v3 search/projects endpoint throughout (no UI scraping, no credentials). 71 distinct queries executed, every one returning HTTP 200 with a parseable JSON array — no login wall, no CAPTCHA, no rate limiting, no API error at any point. Capped result sets (pageSize=100) were paginated to exhaustion: "oligonucleotide" 197 projects, "siRNA" 379, "ASO" 45, "aptamer" 57. All responses were pooled into 1,116 unique project records and screened programmatically against a regex intersection of oligonucleotide-therapeutic vocabulary (antisense, ASO, siRNA, phosphorothioate, gapmer, GalNAc, morpholino, LNA, 2'-MOE/methoxyethyl) and coagulation vocabulary (coagulat*, coagulopath*, aPTT, thromboplastin, thrombin, platelet, h(a)emostas*, fibrinogen, prothrombin, factor XI/XII, kallikrein, antithrombin, thrombocytopen*, thrombosis/thrombotic, anti-Xa, ROTEM, thromboelast*, fibrin, clotting, INR) over title, project description, sample-processing protocol, data-processing protocol and keywords.

INTERSECTION RESULT: 6 dual-vocabulary hits, all adjudicated FALSE POSITIVES and excluded. PXD042701, PXD047517, PXD052978 and PXD053014 match "GalNAc" as N-acetylgalactosamine O-glycosylation (glycoproteomics), not GalNAc-conjugated siRNA; their coagulation terms are incidental substrate names ("fibrinogen", "hemostasis"). PXD037158 (mouse thrombospondin O-fucosylation, platelet trafficking) and PXD063570 (rat FBXW7/MYRF myelin) use siRNA purely as a laboratory knockdown reagent with no coagulation measurement.

ZERO HITS FOR EVERY NAMED COMPOUND except nusinersen: mipomersen, volanesorsen, inotersen, olezarsen, eplontersen, donidalorsen, fitusiran, custirsen, pegnivacogin, defibrotide, patisiran, inclisiran, givosiran, lumasiran, vutrisiran, revusiran, nedosiran, eteplirsen, golodirsen all returned 0 records. Nusinersen returned 6 records (PXD016757, PXD047529, PXD051600, PXD054900, PXD060060, PXD065345) — all CSF biomarker/treatment-response proteomics in SMA patients. These are human, and nusinersen is in the clinically dosed set, but CSF proteome profiling yields no coagulation assay, no sequence, no chemistry map and no purity data, so none closes a gap and none is reported above.

GAP 5 (named acquisition targets) is categorically out of scope for PRIDE: ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245, the volanesorsen APPROACH appendix (ISIS 304801-CS6) and the mipomersen CS5/CS7/CS12 safety tables are clinical-trial documents with no MS proteomics component and are not deposited in, nor linkable from, a proteomics archive.

API CAVEATS worth recording for other endpoints. (1) Multi-word keywords are AND-ed across indexed fields, so "siRNA coagulation", "oligonucleotide coagulation", "antisense platelet" and similar genuinely return 0 rather than erroring — these zeros are real, not a query-syntax artefact. (2) The keyword match is substring-based and produces spurious hits on short tokens: "IONIS" returned 50 records by matching inside "ionisation"/"ionization", and "TEG" matches inside "integrated"/"strategy". An earlier loose screen inflated to 257 apparent hits purely from these substring artefacts; the tightened word-boundary regex reduced it to the 6 adjudicated above. Any downstream worker reusing this resource should use word-boundary matching.

RECOMMENDATION: mark PRIDE closed and do not re-query. Oligonucleotide-protein binding mechanism work of the PXD068788 type is better pursued through its primary publication (Mol Ther Nucleic Acids, DOI 10.1016/J.OMTN.2026.102832, where any sequence table would be in supplementary material) than through the archive. Effort for gaps 1-2 is better spent on Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 and the FDA/EMA review-document route.

coverage_log.applicability: ProteomeXchange is a mass-spectrometry proteomics data archive: its unit of deposit is raw/processed MS files plus sample metadata, so it structurally cannot hold coagulation function endpoints (aPTT, PT/INR, thrombin generation, anti-Xa, TEG/ROTEM), oligonucleotide sequences, per-position chemistry annotation, or drug-substance purity certificates — none of these are proteomics data types and none have a field in the PX/PRIDE metadata schema. I searched it exhaustively anyway and confirmed the empirical result matches: across all 56,879 datasets in all six partner repositories (PRIDE 41,379; iProX 8,084; MassIVE 3,649; jPOST 3,153; PanoramaPublic 474; PeptideAtlas 140) there is ZERO intersection between the oligonucleotide-therapeutic literature and the coagulation literature. The archive holds ~25 oligonucleotide datasets (all CNS/CSF pharmacodynamics, intracellular interactome, or aptamer delivery) and ~90 coagulation datasets (all disease-biomarker plasma/clot proteomics, biomaterial contact activation, or protease specificity) and not one record belongs to both sets. Every targeted intersection query returned 0 rows, as did every named drug (volanesorsen, inotersen, mipomersen, fitusiran, olezarsen, donidalorsen, eplontersen, custirsen, pegnivacogin, defibrotide) and every coagulation assay term (aPTT, activated partial thromboplastin, anti-Xa, thromboelastography, prekallikrein). The two named acquisition targets in Gap 5 (NCT03417245 ATLAS-A/B, APPROACH ISIS 304801-CS6, mipomersen CS5/CS7/CS12) are clinical trial documents and cannot exist here. Recommendation: close ProteomeXchange out of the acquisition plan for the coagulopathy endpoint — it is a structural zero, not a search-depth problem, and re-running it later will not change the answer.

results.authors_year: Submitter record, PRIDE; publication DOI 10.1016/J.OMTN.2026.102832 (Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids, 2026)

results.why_relevant: REPORTED AS CONTEXT ONLY — closes no gap. This is the single record in the whole archive that systematically compares phosphorothioate backbone chemistries (tcDNA vs LNA vs 2'-MOE) for protein binding in a human system, and it varies sequence independently of chemistry (SSOEx51 vs TSB-T3 vs TSB-C1). Protein avidity of the PS backbone is the accepted upstream mechanism for contact-pathway activation, so this is the closest mechanistic neighbour ProteomeXchange contains. But the readout is intracellular trafficking partners, not coagulation function: no aPTT, no thrombin generation, no plasma or platelet system, no donors, no coagulation factor endpoint. The per-chemistry construct definitions live in the open-access MTNA paper, not in the PX metadata, so even the chemistry-annotation value is a publication lead rather than an archive asset.

results.title: Profiling the interactome of oligonucleotide drugs by proximity biotinylation
results.authors_year: Stafforst lab; publication DOI 10.1038/S41589-023-01530-Z (Nature Chemical Biology, 2024); PX announced 2024-10-22
results.species_and_system: Homo sapiens — live human cells, BASU proximity biotinylation + SILAC, 76/90 files. Human in vitro, intracellular; NOT plasma, whole blood or platelets.
results.why_relevant: REPORTED AS CONTEXT ONLY — closes no gap. The largest oligonucleotide-drug protein-interaction resource in the archive (with sibling records PXD079777 and PXD066763 from the same lab). Catalogues which human proteins therapeutic oligos engage, which is the general mechanism class that contact activation sits inside. However it measures in-cell proximity partners, not coagulation function, and does not touch the contact pathway, FXII/FXI/prekallikrein, or any plasma system. Included so the coverage log records that the archive's flagship oligo-interactome dataset was found and assessed and judged non-qualifying, rather than appearing unsearched.

coverage_log.notes:
METHOD: Used the PROXI REST API as instructed (no UI scraping, no credentials). Verified before concluding that the `search` parameter indexes dataset DESCRIPTIONS and not just titles/keywords — `search=phosphorothioate` returns 3 rows where `keywords=phosphorothioate` returns 0 — so the null intersection result reflects a genuine full-text sweep, not a shallow title match. Verified index completeness via the repository facet on an unfiltered query: 56,879 datasets across all six PX partner repositories, so MassIVE, jPOST, iProX, PanoramaPublic and PeptideAtlas are all covered by these queries and need no separate search.

NO BARRIERS. Every query executed and returned a parsed result set. HTTP 200 throughout, no login wall, no CAPTCHA, no rate limiting, no proxy interference.

TWO FALSE-POSITIVE TRAPS CHECKED AND CLEARED, so nobody re-runs these and thinks something was missed:
- `search=GalNAc` returns 28 rows, which looks promising for GalNAc-conjugated siRNA. All 28 are O-linked glycosylation / GalNAc-transferase glycobiology (GALNT isoforms, Tn/T antigen mapping, plant lectins). Zero are GalNAc-siRNA conjugates.
- `search=ROTEM` returns 58 rows, which looks promising for viscoelastic testing. All are spurious fuzzy/substring matches on unrelated titles (flagellar filament supercoiling, MRSA beta-lactam susceptome, nucleic-acid-binding protein DIA). Zero are thromboelastometry.

OLIGONUCLEOTIDE DATASETS FOUND AND REJECTED (full inventory, so this is auditable): PXD079777, PXD066763, PXD045992 (Stafforst oligo-drug interactomes, human cells); PXD068788 (PS-SSO chemistry AP-MS, human muscle cells); PXD055796 (human post-mortem spinal cord from 6 BIIB078-treated c9ALS trial patients — a genuine human ASO trial tissue set, but CNS target engagement only, no blood endpoint, and BIIB078's sequence is not disclosed in the record); PXD053387 (tau ASO, mouse brain); PXD061252/61254/61255/61258/61261 (Shank2/Shank3 ASO, mouse brain); PXD031432 (PrP ASO pharmacodynamics, human + rat CSF/brain); PXD016757, PXD054900, PXD065345 (nusinersen, human CSF); PXD049295, PXD034982, PXD055162, PXD082487 (aptamer delivery/targeting, mostly mouse); PXD008819-23 (SOMAmer enrichment confirmation, human plasma/serum/urine — aptamer reagents for assay QC, not therapeutics, no coagulation readout). Not one reports a coagulation endpoint.

COAGULATION DATASETS FOUND AND REJECTED: ~90 records, all one of three kinds — (a) disease-biomarker plasma/serum/EV proteomics where "complement and coagulation cascades" is a KEGG enrichment hit (long COVID, sepsis, TB, atrial fibrillation, dermatomyositis, gestational diabetes, SLE, schizophrenia); (b) biomaterial haemocompatibility (PXD054476 antithrombotic coating controlling FXII contact activation, PXD024284 Nitinol, PXD024170 zeolite, PXD044005 anticoagulant sponge) — these are the only true contact-activation mechanism datasets but the activator is a surface, never an oligonucleotide; (c) coagulation protease biochemistry (PXD018976 high-throughput specificity profiling of blood coagulation proteases, PXD039489 thrombin activation of the FXI dimer, PXD020319/20320/20321/22959 octapeptide substrate quantification). PXD018976 and PXD039489 use purified human coagulation factors and would be relevant IF an oligonucleotide had been tested in them — it was not; the perturbants are peptide substrates and salts.

WHY THIS IS A STRUCTURAL ZERO, NOT A SEARCH FAILURE: the Phase 2 criteria the dataset is being ranked against (sequence of every oligo, location of every chemical modification, purity and characterisation of each) are attributes of a drug substance. ProteomeXchange's metadata schema has no field for any of them, and its deposits are MS instrument output. A proteomics archive is the wrong shape for this endpoint in principle, and the exhaustive search confirms it is also empty in practice. Suggest marking this resource CLOSED/NOT-APPLICABLE in the coverage log with no re-run scheduled. If an oligonucleotide-plus-coagulation proteomics study is ever wanted, the productive route is the primary literature via Europe PMC/PubMed, with ProteomeXchange checked only as a data-availability follow-up on a specific paper's accession.

coverage_log.applicability: BioStudies applies, but in a narrower way than its front page suggests, and this shapes how its output should be used. For this endpoint it is not an independent discovery index: every relevant record returned carries an S-EPMC accession, meaning it is a mirror of Europe PMC article metadata whose added value is file-level access to the supplementary material. Probes restricted to the native submitted-study collection ('oligonucleotide', 'antisense AND oligonucleotide', 'siRNA AND toxicity' with collection=BioStudies) returned 0 hits, and a 100-record prefix census over 'antisense AND oligonucleotide AND coagulation' (25 hits), 'oligonucleotide AND hemostasis' (37) and 'antisense AND platelet AND toxicity' (5) found only S-EPMC records plus two irrelevant ArrayExpress transcriptomics sets (E-GEOD-45627, E-GEOD-20985). So there are no native S-BSST or ArrayExpress oligonucleotide-coagulation datasets to harvest. Treat BioStudies as a supplementary-file retrieval layer for records discovered in Europe PMC — which is genuinely valuable here, because gaps 3 and 4 live in supplementary tables, and BioStudies exposes them as individually addressable URLs with declared byte sizes.
coverage_log.notes:
ACCESS AND METHOD. Fully open: no login, no CAPTCHA, no rate limiting encountered, no API key. Search via /api/v1/search?query=...&pageSize=..., records via /api/v1/studies/{accession}, files via /biostudies/files/{accession}/{path}. File endpoints answer HTTP 302, so curl needs -L; without it you get a 0-byte file and could wrongly log a barrier. Four downloads verified byte-exact: S-EPMC4367537 (339,044), S-EPMC6386089 (35,192), S-EPMC8820988 (460,570), S-EPMC10143489 (281,718).

QUERY-SYNTAX TRAP, important for anyone repeating this. The default parser ORs bare terms, so natural-language queries are useless: 'antisense oligonucleotide coagulation' returned 33,752 hits and 'APPROACH volanesorsen' 38,420. Double-quoting does NOT force a phrase for alphanumeric identifiers — "ISIS 304801" returned 1,105 hits topped by papers about Islamic State and the whale Basilosaurus isis. Explicit AND between every term is required; that is the form used for all combined queries above. Subscript markup also defeats matching: 'IONIS-FXIRx' returns 0 hits even though the IONIS-FXIRx ESRD trial is in the archive, because the title stores FXI<sub>Rx</sub>.

NAMED ACQUISITION TARGETS (target 5) — mostly negative, stated plainly:
- ATLAS-A/B primary publication, NCT03417245: NOT in BioStudies. 'ATLAS-A/B' = 0 hits; 'NCT03417245' = 30 hits but all conference abstracts and reviews with 0 files. Only ATLAS-PPX (S-EPMC11181353), ATLAS-OLE (S-EPMC12824673) and the phase 1 inhibitor cohort (S-EPMC8251589, JTH-19-1436-s001.docx read: CONSORT diagram and AST/ALT traces only, no coagulation tables) are present.
- Volanesorsen APPROACH supplementary appendix (ISIS 304801-CS6): NOT present. 19 volanesorsen records exist but none is the APPROACH primary. Closest is S-EPMC9788245 (pooled analysis, ECI-52-e13841-s001.doc, 349,696 bytes, read: 1 platelet mention, 4 adverse-event mentions — thin) and S-EPMC7415887, a thorough-QT study in 52 healthy volunteers with five separate supplements including three standalone table PDFs, which may carry per-subject laboratory data.
- Mipomersen CS5/CS7/CS12 individual safety tables: only partly. S-EPMC3496741 (severe hypercholesterolemia on maximally tolerated therapy) holds pone.0049006.s001.doc — read, and it is only a CONSORT checklist — plus an unread pone.0049006.s002.pdf of 2,734,672 bytes that is large enough to be the full trial protocol and is the one item here worth opening next. S-EPMC3751967 (statin-intolerant, Eur Heart J) holds supp_ehs023_ehs023supp_table.doc (74,752 bytes) and a figure doc. No record matching RADICHOL II was found ('RADICHOL' returns 1 unrelated oncology hit).

DATA-QUALITY DEFECT WORTH PROPAGATING. S-EPMC12451317, the fitusiran coagulation-assay interference paper and on title the single most on-point gap-1 record in the archive, has a mismatched attachment: its mmc1.docx contains a PubMed search strategy on artificial intelligence and dental caries. I confirmed this by extracting the document XML, not by inference. Anyone harvesting BioStudies supplements programmatically should content-validate rather than trust the accession-to-file mapping, and this paper's real appendix must come from the publisher.

VERIFICATION LIMIT, disclosed. I could read DOCX supplements directly (zipfile plus XML) and legacy .doc via strings, and those reads are the basis for the 'VERIFIED' claims on S-EPMC7292364, S-EPMC5697752, S-EPMC12451317, S-EPMC8251589, S-EPMC3496741 and S-EPMC9788245. I could NOT extract text from the PDF supplements: pypdf and pdfminer.six both abort in this container because the system cryptography module raises a pyo3 PanicException (no _cffi_backend), and poppler-utils could not be installed. This is a local tooling limitation, not a BioStudies barrier — the PDFs downloaded intact. Claims about PDF contents above are therefore marked as inferred or unverified, and the 'MOE: 19' observation for S-EPMC8820988 comes from a crude zlib stream scan, which is suggestive but not proof.

SUGGESTED NEXT ACTIONS. Highest value per unit effort: open pone.0049006.s002.pdf (mipomersen protocol), the five S-EPMC7415887 volanesorsen supplements, and the S-EPMC10143489 minipig supplementary PDF to settle whether a human arm exists and so whether the gap-2 bridge is real. Also note that the four aptamer records (S-EPMC5818257, S-EPMC5697752, S-EPMC3636572, S-EPMC7868722) are collectively the densest source of human in vitro coagulation data with printed sequences found anywhere in this archive; if the dataset's 218 compounds are antisense- and siRNA-only, a scope decision is needed on whether aptamers count as oligonucleotides for this submission before these are ingested.

coverage_log.applicability: ArrayExpress is a gene-expression archive: its records hold array/RNA-seq intensity and count matrices with IDF/SDRF experiment metadata, and it has no data model for the functional coagulation endpoints this dataset is built from (aPTT, PT/INR, thrombin generation, anti-Xa, TEG/ROTEM, platelet counts, contact-pathway activation), so it cannot close Gap 1 or Gap 2 in the sense required, and it carries no drug-development documentation (purity certificates, trial appendices) so it cannot close Gap 4 or Gap 5 at all. It is also structurally weak for Gap 3: oligonucleotide identity in SDRF files is recorded as a free-text compound label, and across the entire collection I found no record printing an oligo sequence or per-position chemistry. Confirming zero coverage for the named acquisition targets (ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245, APPROACH ISIS 304801-CS6, mipomersen CS5/CS7/CS12) and for every clinically dosed coagulation-relevant oligo is nevertheless a genuine negative result worth logging, because it rules this archive out as a bridge source.
