results.title: Regulation of Coagulation Factor XI expression by MicroRNAs in the Human Liver
results.authors_year: Salloum-Asfar S, Martínez C et al., Centro Regional de Hemodonación, Universidad de Murcia; released 2014
results.species_and_system: Homo sapiens — total RNA from human livers (4 samples, DONOR as the experimental factor); companion work transfected HepG2 cells with miRNA mimics to modulate FXI
results.why_relevant: The single record returned by a quoted '"factor XI"' query across the entire collection (totalHits=1), and the only hemostasis-target record in the archive. It establishes human-liver miRNA/FXI regulatory baseline, which is directionally interesting because FXI is the target of the IONIS-FXIRx / fesomersen programme that sits in the coagulation dataset. It does NOT close any listed gap: the oligonucleotides involved are miRNA mimics/inhibitors used as research reagents rather than clinical constructs, no sequences or chemistries are deposited, the archived data are liver miRNA/mRNA profiles not coagulation assays, and nothing bridges to an animal system. Logged because the negative result is informative — even the one FXI-tagged record in ArrayExpress carries no oligo coagulation toxicity measurement.

coverage_log.notes:
METHOD. Used the BioStudies REST API throughout, never the web UI; no login, no CAPTCHA, no rate limiting, no TLS problem. Three endpoints: collection-scoped search (GET /biostudies/api/v1/arrayexpress/search?query=...&pageSize=...), study metadata (GET /biostudies/api/v1/studies/{accession}), and the raw SDRF over the files service (GET -L /biostudies/files/{acc}/{acc}.sdrf.txt). 59 queries executed against the ArrayExpress collection, all returning results pages I read. One control query was run at whole-BioStudies scope first to verify the API was live; I then stayed collection-scoped, because unscoped BioStudies search mixes in tens of thousands of S-EPMC literature stubs that belong to a different resource and would have inflated this log falsely.

SEARCH-ENGINE CAVEAT worth recording for whoever repeats this. BioStudies free-text search is OR-combining and matches array-platform boilerplate, so the bare token "oligonucleotide" returns ~4,000-6,000 hits that are almost entirely microarray-design papers ("oligonucleotide microarray", "long oligonucleotide array") with no oligonucleotide test article at all. Multi-word queries are therefore near-useless here: 'thrombocytopenia oligonucleotide' (3,979 hits) and 'coagulation oligonucleotide' (4,040 hits) return identical microarray-platform noise in the same rank order. Only quoted phrases and single distinctive tokens discriminate. All the discriminating counts below come from quoted or single-token queries and are trustworthy.

HARD NEGATIVES — every clinically dosed oligonucleotide in the task vocabulary returns totalHits = 0 in ArrayExpress: volanesorsen 0, inotersen 0, mipomersen 0, fitusiran 0, olezarsen 0, donidalorsen 0, eplontersen 0, custirsen 0, defibrotide 0, pegnivacogin 0. Alnylam 0. So the archive holds no deposit for any compound in the human-dosed subset, and nothing bears on the named Gap 5 acquisition targets (ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245, APPROACH ISIS 304801-CS6, mipomersen ISIS 301012-CS5 / CS7 RADICHOL II / CS12) — expected, since trial safety appendices are not expression data.

HARD NEGATIVES on coagulation assay and mechanism vocabulary: aPTT 0, "contact activation" 0, prekallikrein 0, KLKB1 0, SERPINC1 0, "2-O-methoxyethyl" 0, "phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide" 0, PS-ASO 0. Low-count queries were inspected record by record and none is an oligonucleotide coagulation study: antithrombin 1 hit (E-GEOD-3956, antiangiogenic antithrombin, no oligo); "factor XI" 1 hit (E-GEOD-61219, logged above); clotting 13, hemostasis 17, aptamer 17 (all five aptamer-named records are E-MTAB-6374..6378, "ACE-Scan" DNA-aptamer microarray chemistry — including a thrombin-binding aptamer, E-MTAB-6378 — but these are in vitro array-binding selection experiments on synthetic surfaces, with no plasma, no blood, no clotting readout and no toxicity endpoint, so the thrombin keyword is a false friend); thrombin 26 (all thrombin-as-stimulus endothelial-cell transcriptomics, the reverse direction of interest); coagulopathy 299 (platelet/TTP/ITP patient transcriptomics, no oligonucleotide exposure); phosphorothioate 32 (reviewed: 31 are research-reagent knockdowns or chemistry-of-array records; the one substantive hit is E-GEOD-61473, logged).

GAP-BY-GAP VERDICT. Gap 1 (human in vitro/ex vivo coagulation assays) — not closed, zero records; the archive contains no plasma, whole-blood, platelet-function or purified-factor assay of any kind, for oligonucleotides or otherwise. Gap 2 (human-to-animal bridge of the same construct) — not closed; I probed this directly with cross-species queries and found no record pairing one named construct across a human system and an animal, and no deposit at all for a named clinical construct to bridge. Gap 3 (exact sequence and per-position chemistry) — not closed; across all 59 queries not one record printed an oligo sequence, and I verified this at file level by pulling the SDRFs of the two best candidates: E-GEOD-61473's SDRF describes its test article only as "a TRIB1 specific antisense nucleotide", and E-GEOD-76343's only as "ISIS761932 oligonucleotide" / "ISIS761909 oligonucleotide". ArrayExpress's MAGE-TAB schema has no sequence or modification field for a test compound, so this is a structural limitation of the resource, not a sampling accident. Gap 4 (purity and tested-material characterisation) — not closed and not closable; the archive has no field for % purity, method, identity confirmation or batch, and nothing resembling a certificate of analysis appeared in any record. Gap 5 (named acquisition targets) — zero coverage, as set out above.

RECOMMENDATION. Do not spend further effort on ArrayExpress or on sibling expression archives (GEO, ENA-linked expression collections) for this endpoint: the resource class is mismatched to coagulation functional data, and the two records I logged as near-misses (E-GEOD-61473, E-GEOD-76343) are worth keeping only as (a) a human-hepatocyte PS/2'-MOE transcriptional background reference and (b) an ISIS-compound-number cross-reference anchor. Neither should be counted as a measurement source, and I would not add any of the three to the dataset as evidence. Gaps 1-4 need pharmacology and clinical-pharmacology literature plus regulatory review documents (FDA/EMA pharmacology reviews and clinical pharmacology summaries carry the aPTT tables, and sponsor patents carry the per-position chemistry) rather than any expression archive.

results.authors_year: Ionis Pharmaceuticals; Phase 2, completed; results posted; protocol+SAP dated 2018-06-14

coverage_log.applicability: Partially applicable, and more so than expected. ClinicalTrials.gov registers human interventional and observational studies, not bench assays, so it cannot supply gap 1 in its strict sense (human plasma/platelet/purified-factor in vitro assays) or gap 2 (human-to-animal bridge of the same construct) or gap 4 (purity, % purity with method, batch analysis) — targeted queries confirmed this rather than assumed it: 'oligonucleotide OR antisense OR siRNA' crossed with query.outc='thrombin generation' returned 0, crossed with thromboelastography/thromboelastometry/ROTEM returned 0, and the 'ex vivo' + contact-activation/thrombin-generation term query returned 0. What the resource does deliver strongly is (a) human trial coagulopathy endpoints with exact per-arm denominators from posted results, including aPTT and FXI percent-change curves, platelet counts, D-dimer and prothrombin fragment 1.2, and ROTEM in one case, and (b) gap 3 — the sponsor protocol PDFs attached to Ionis and Sanofi records contain a 'Chemistry' section giving full position-level modification patterns for clinically dosed oligos, which is the single highest-value thing this registry holds for a Phase 2 submission.
coverage_log.notes:
RANKED BY PHASE 2 CRITERIA, NOT ROW VOLUME. The ordering above puts the one ex vivo viscoelastic/thrombin-marker record first, then human trial endpoints with dose-stratified denominators, then the chemistry-bearing protocol documents, then forward-watch records.

THE SINGLE MOST REUSABLE FINDING — a general, repeatable route to gap 3. Every Ionis-sponsored protocol PDF posted on ClinicalTrials.gov contains a numbered section 2.3.2 'Chemistry' that states, in extractable prose, the oligomer length, that all internucleoside linkages are phosphorothioate, the exact count and position of the 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) wings and the deoxynucleotide gap, any GalNAc endcap chemistry, and the target mRNA base coordinates. Verified verbatim on three independent drugs: inotersen/ISIS 420915 (20-mer, all-PS, 5 MOE + 10 DNA + 5 MOE, TTR 3'UTR), volanesorsen (20-mer, all-PS, 5-10-5 MOE gapmer, apoC-III 3'UTR positions 489-508), olezarsen/ISIS 678354 (20-mer, all-PS, 5-10-5 MOE gapmer plus a 5'-trishexylamino-(THA)-C6-GalNAc3 endcap, apoC-III positions 489-508). Volanesorsen and olezarsen share the identical target site, so the dataset gains a matched unconjugated-vs-GalNAc chemistry pair against one target. Confirmed Prot or Prot_SAP PDFs are available on at least: NCT01737398 and NCT02175004 (inotersen), NCT02658175 and NCT02527343 (volanesorsen), NCT04568434, NCT05355402, NCT03385239 (olezarsen), NCT03728634 and NCT04136184 (eplontersen), NCT04307381 and NCT04030598 (donidalorsen), NCT03358030 (IONIS-FXIRx), NCT04534114 (fesomersen), NCT03417245, NCT03417102, NCT03549871 (fitusiran), NCT02876601 (defibrotide). Document URL pattern, confirmed working: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/{last two digits of the NCT number}/{NCTID}/{filename}.pdf — all six I tested returned HTTP 200 application/pdf with no authentication.

NAMED ACQUISITION TARGETS — status. ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245: FOUND, primary publication resolved to Srivastava et al. Lancet Haematol 2023;10(5):e322-e332 PMID 37003278 from the record's own reference module, posted results serve as the safety appendix, protocol and SAP PDFs open. Volanesorsen APPROACH, sponsor protocol ISIS 304801-CS6: trial FOUND as NCT02211209 with posted results and primary publication PMID 31390500, but the protocol/SAP is NOT posted on that record — use the APPROACH-OLE record NCT02658175 (ISIS 304801-CS7) whose protocol carries the same section 2.3.2 Chemistry, or BROADEN NCT02527343. Mipomersen ISIS 301012-CS5, CS7, CS12: all three FOUND and mapped by sponsor protocol ID to NCT00607373, NCT00706849 (Stein et al. 2012, PMID 23060426) and NCT00770146, all with posted safety tables, none with a posted protocol. NOTE on labelling: the task calls CS7 'RADICHOL II'; the registry's org study ID 301012-CS7 maps to NCT00706849, titled as the FH-with-coronary-artery-disease add-on study, so that alias should be verified against the sponsor's own naming before it is carried into the dataset.

NEAR-MISSES AND FORWARD-WATCH RECORDS NOT IN THE TWELVE, all open_access registry records: NCT03582462 (ION 957943-CS1, IONIS FXI-LRx, n=66 healthy volunteers, SAD/MAD, outcomes include change from baseline in FXI antigen, FXI activity, aPTT, PT and INR — the best-designed healthy-volunteer coagulation panel for a GalNAc FXI ASO, but NO results posted). NCT04549922 (ASKCOV, ISIS 721744 / donidalorsen in COVID-19, n=111, investigator-initiated, outcomes include aPTT, PT, fibrinogen and D-dimer over the first 15 days — directly on the contact/kallikrein pathway named in gap 1, but NO results posted). NCT01713361 (ISIS 416858-CS3, ISIS-FXIRx vs enoxaparin in total knee arthroplasty, n=315, the Buller NEJM 2015 study and the largest oligo VTE-endpoint trial found; NO results posted and no protocol). NCT02553889 (ISIS 416858-CS4, ESRD, n=49, aPTT absolute and percent change plus PT/INR as secondary outcomes; NO results posted). NCT05071300 (eplontersen ISIS/ION-682884-CS13, n=151) and NCT05667493 (ION-682884-CS12, n=1400) both carry 'Change From Baseline in Platelet Count' as a PRIMARY outcome and CS13 adds 'Number of Participants With Clinically Significant Changes From Baseline in Coagulation Tests'; neither has posted results yet. NCT05844293 (SRN-122, FXI-GalNAc-siRNA single ascending dose in healthy subjects, n=40, Chinese sponsor) and NCT07655427 (SRSD107-102, n=48, PT/aPTT/FXI activity/FXI antigen) are newer FXI siRNA entrants worth tracking. NCT06669234 (ALN-F1202, n=56, aPTT and PT change), NCT07081503 (ADX-626) and NCT07430397 (CITY-FXI, n=182) extend the same FXI-lowering class.

NEGATIVE RESULTS WORTH RECORDING SO THEY ARE NOT RE-SEARCHED. Among oligonucleotide/aptamer trials WITH posted results, exactly one — NCT03358030 — has an aPTT, anti-Xa or PT outcome measure carrying actual data; the query 'oligonucleotide OR antisense OR siRNA OR aptamer' x query.outc='activated partial thromboplastin time' OR 'anti-Xa' OR 'prothrombin time' x aggFilters=results:with returned only three studies and the other two (NCT03981419 GRF6021, NCT02128958 CF102) are not oligonucleotides. A free-text search on 'phosphorothioate' returns 11 studies and none adds coagulation data beyond what is listed above. The REG1 aptamer system (pegnivacogin/anivamersen) is registered across NCT01848106 (REGULATE-PCI, terminated, n=3232), NCT00932100 (n=640), NCT00715455, NCT01872572 and NCT00113997, but NOT ONE of the five has posted results, so despite being the largest anticoagulant-aptamer programme on the registry it yields no extractable rows here — its data must come from the journal literature instead. Custirsen (OGX-011) has 13 registered trials, two with posted results (NCT00327340, NCT00138658), but no coagulation outcome measures; it is an oncology programme and contributes nothing to this endpoint. Defibrotide returns 8 trials with posted results but only NCT02876601 measures coagulation mechanistically; the veno-occlusive-disease trials (NCT02851407, NCT00358501, NCT00628498, NCT03339297, NCT03384693) report platelet engraftment and bleeding-related discontinuation only.

GAP 4 (purity and tested-material characterisation): ZERO. No registry record and none of the six protocol PDFs I extracted contains a % purity figure with method, an identity-confirmation statement, or a batch/certificate-of-analysis reference. Keyword scans for 'purity', 'certificate of analysis', 'drug substance' and 'molecular weight' across the inotersen, ISIS 416858-CS5, ATLAS-A/B, volanesorsen-OLE and olezarsen-CS3 protocols returned only incidental matches (e.g. 'low molecular weight heparin'). This gap cannot be closed from ClinicalTrials.gov and should be routed to regulatory sources (FDA/EMA quality assessment reports, DMF summaries) or to the sponsors' CMC publications.

GAP 2 (human-to-animal bridge): ZERO direct hits, with one partial. The ATLAS-A/B protocol states that the fitusiran siRNA sequence is homologous across all tested non-human primates, which establishes that the same construct was given to humans and to NHPs — a construct-identity bridge, but the protocol carries no NHP coagulation measurements, so the animal half must come from elsewhere.

coverage_log.barrier: PARTIAL BARRIER. Every interactive and API endpoint under ctdbase.org is behind an ALTCHA proof-of-work human-verification wall: GET /tools/batchQuery.go, /basicQuery.go and /detail.go all return "HTTP/1.1 302 Moved Temporarily" (Content-Length 2774, Server nginx/1.30.4, X-Powered-By Express) serving a page containing 'To continue, we need to verify you are a human' and '<altcha-widget challengeurl="/captcha.go?altcha=yes">', plus the text 'If you are having trouble accessing computationally from any device, please use a browser to access CTD from that device and complete the captcha verification.' Tried: plain curl, and curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent; both 302 identically. I did NOT attempt to solve or bypass the challenge. CTD has no documented REST/JSON API, so batchQuery.go is its only query API and it is unusable here. WORKAROUND THAT SUCCEEDED: the bulk report directory https://ctdbase.org/reports/ is NOT captcha-walled (HTTP 200). coverage_log.applicability: CTD can only partially apply. It is a curated chemical-gene-disease association database built on MeSH vocabularies; it stores no assay measurements (no aPTT seconds, no thrombin-generation curves, no donor counts, no assay conditions), has no purity or tested-material characterisation fields at all, and does not index clinical trials or protocol appendices — so Phase 2 gaps 4 (purity/characterisation) and 5 (ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245, volanesorsen APPROACH appendix, mipomersen CS5/CS7/CS12 safety tables) cannot be served by this resource in principle. Its real, narrow value here is its MeSH-derived chemical vocabulary, which encodes exact nucleotide sequence plus uniform backbone chemistry for a handful of clinically dosed phosphorothioate oligos (gap 3), and its DirectEvidence chemical-disease curation, which surfaced one usable human trial with coagulation endpoints (gap 1). On the central gap it is empty: across 29 USAN-stem oligo drugs and 8 oligonucleotide class terms (478 interaction rows), CTD curates ZERO interactions with any of 48 coagulation or platelet genes and ZERO blood-coagulation/platelet GO phenotypes.

results.why_relevant: The one genuinely valuable study record CTD surfaced, and the only oligo-coagulopathy record in the whole database with curated DirectEvidence. The paper itself is a human interventional trial whose PRIMARY pharmacodynamic endpoint is aPTT: the abstract alone prints dose-level medians with 25th/75th percentiles at 10 min post-bolus — 29.2 s (28.1, 29.8), 34.6 s (30.9, 40.0), 46.9 s (40.3, 51.1), 52.2 s (46.3, 58.6), P<0.0001 — plus antidote reversal, so usable numeric coagulation endpoints are extractable even without full text. results.title: Thymidine-phosphorothioate oligonucleotides induce activation and apoptosis of CLL cells independently of CpG motifs or BCL-2 gene interference
results.authors_year: Castro JE, Prada CE, Aguillon RA, Kitada S, Fukuda T, Motta M, Wu C, Dicker F, Sun G, Wang JY, Carson DA, Reed JC, Kipps TJ — Leukemia 2006;20(4):680-8
results.species_and_system: Human ex vivo primary cells in vitro: primary chronic lymphocytic leukemia B cells from patients, treated with matched phosphorothioate (PS-ODN) versus phosphodiester (PO-ODN) oligonucleotides including G3139/oblimersen.
results.why_relevant: Not a coagulation assay, so it closes no coagulation gap — included because it is the single cleanest BACKBONE-ATTRIBUTION control in CTD's oligo curation and is directly reusable as methodological support. It is a human primary-cell experiment that isolates the phosphorothioate backbone itself as the causal agent: effects occurred with PS-ODN but not sequence-matched PO-ODN, and were independent of both the antisense sequence and CpG motifs. That is the same backbone-versus-sequence logic needed to attribute aPTT prolongation to the PS backbone rather than to target knockdown, in the same species and with a donor-derived human system. Cited by CTD as the source for its Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotides (D054735) chem-gene rows on BAX, BCL2, BID and TP53.

On its face this is the most attractive oligo-coagulopathy hit in CTD: imetelstat is a thio-phosphoramidate oligonucleotide, it causes clinically important thrombocytopenia, and this is CTD's only curated DirectEvidence 'marker/mechanism' link from an oligo to Thromboembolism. coverage_log.notes:
ACCESS ROUTE. CTD's query API and web UI are captcha-walled (see barrier), so all queries ran locally against the complete 2026-09-29 bulk release pulled from the open https://ctdbase.org/reports/ directory. Local working files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Works/2c752835-a5be-5204-bb06-a9e7affc8fc6/scratchpad (CTD_chemicals.tsv.gz, CTD_chem_gene_ixns.tsv.gz, CTD_pheno.tsv.gz, and the filtered extracts oligo_chemgene.tsv, oligo_disease_all.tsv, oligo_coag_disease.tsv, oligo_disease2.tsv, oligo_pheno.tsv, stem_ids_fix.tsv). CTD's licence requires citation, hyperlinks back to CTD data pages from any context using its data, and notifying CTD of use — relevant if these four sequence records go into a public Phase 2 release.

THE CENTRAL NEGATIVE, AND IT IS A STRONG ONE. CTD curates ZERO oligonucleotide interactions with coagulation biology. Specifics: (a) 29 chemicals matching USAN oligo stems are in the vocabulary, but only 6 have ANY curated chem-gene interaction — 8 rows total, all on-target pharmacology (eteplirsen/golodirsen/viltolarsen x DMD splicing, mipomersen x APOB, oblimersen x BCL2/CASP3/APP, eluforsen x CFTR); zero rows against a 48-gene coagulation/platelet panel. (b) The 8 oligonucleotide CLASS terms (D054735 Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotides 17 rows, D020319 antisense ODN 44, D020320 antisense ORN 62, D009841 Oligonucleotides 9, D009838 ODN 23, D052157 Nucleotide Aptamers 15, D060172 Morpholinos 1, C408982 CpG-ODN 307 = 478 rows) yield zero coagulation-gene interactions; D054735's complete gene list is BAX, BCL2, BID, TP53, CXCL10, IL1B, IRAK4, MYD88, RELA, TERT, TLR7, TLR8, TNF. (c) Zero coagulation GO phenotypes for any oligo chemical, across 69 oligo phenotype rows.

THAT ABSENCE IS REAL, NOT A SCHEMA LIMIT. I ran a deliberate capability control: CTD does carry coagulation phenotypes in quantity for other chemicals — 216 rows 'platelet aggregation', 87 'blood coagulation', 54 'blood coagulation, fibrin clot formation', 52 'positive regulation of blood coagulation', 51 'positive regulation of platelet aggregation', 49 'platelet activation', plus fibrinolysis and haemostasis terms. So CTD can represent exactly the endpoints we need and simply has not curated them for oligonucleotides. This is a defensible, citable statement of the field's curation gap rather than a tooling failure, and it supports the Phase 2 argument that a purpose-built oligo coagulopathy dataset does not duplicate existing public resources.

MOST ON-POINT COMPOUND IS AN EMPTY STUB. ISIS 416858 (MESH:C572197, synonym 'FXI-ASO', i.e. IONIS-FXI-Rx) — the factor XI ASO, the single most relevant compound in the gap list — exists in CTD's vocabulary with ZERO chem-gene rows, ZERO chem-disease rows and ZERO phenotype rows. Same vocabulary-only status for volanesorsen (as 'ISIS 304801', MESH:C000593612), inotersen, olezarsen, donidalorsen, eplontersen, fitusiran, pelacarsen, vupanorsen, custirsen (as 'OGX-011'), nusinersen, tofersen, tominersen, alicaforsen, apatorsen, casimersen, danvatirsen, cobomarsen, cenersen, miravirsen, radavirsen, aprinocarsen and AKCEA-APO(a)-LRx. Patisiran, inclisiran, lumasiran, nedosiran, vutrisiran and revusiran are absent from CTD entirely. Do not spend further effort on CTD for these.

BEWARE THE INFERRED ROWS — THEY LOOK LIKE EVIDENCE AND ARE NOT. Of 3,846 oligo chem-disease rows retrieved, only 28 carry DirectEvidence; 49 rows have coagulopathy-type disease names and all but 3 have an EMPTY DirectEvidence field, meaning CTD inferred them statistically from a shared gene (TNF, IL6, IL1B, MMP9, VEGFA, KDR, CASP3, BCL2). Examples: 'Phosphorothioate Oligonucleotides x Venous Thromboembolism, inference gene TNF, score 3.77, PMID 22473048' and 'mipomersen x Hemorrhage, inference gene APOB, score 5.16, PMID 31186542'. The attached PMIDs document the GENE-disease link, not the chemical-coagulopathy link, so citing them as oligo coagulopathy evidence would be a misattribution. Filter on DirectEvidence being non-empty before ingesting anything from CTD. After that filter, the entire database contains exactly three oligo-coagulopathy rows: the pegnivacogin/Hematoma row (result 5, genuine), the imetelstat/Thromboembolism row (result 7, a curation error), and 'defibrotide x Shock, Hemorrhagic, therapeutic, PMID 3063971' — which I verified as Bitterman, Lefer & Lefer, Naunyn Schmiedebergs Arch Pharmacol 1988, a RAT haemorrhagic-shock study about prostacyclin release and cathepsin D, with no coagulation assay on an oligo; defibrotide is also a polydisperse porcine DNA mixture with no definable sequence, so it cannot satisfy the Phase 2 sequence requirement and I excluded it.

GAPS CTD CANNOT TOUCH. Gap 2 (human-to-animal bridge): CTD does carry an Organism field, so same-construct cross-species comparison is structurally possible, but no oligo has a coagulation endpoint in either species and the only non-human oligo rows are defibrotide in Rattus norvegicus (CTSD export, SELP expression) and a phosphorothioate-class set in Mus musculus (TNF, IL1B, IRAK4, MYD88, RELA from PMID 28363843) — no human counterpart measured, so no bridge. Gap 4 (purity/characterisation): CTD has no field for purity, method, identity confirmation or batch analysis; structurally impossible. Gap 5 (named acquisition targets): CTD does not index clinical trials, NCT numbers, sponsor protocols or supplementary appendices, so NCT03417245 ATLAS-A/B, the volanesorsen APPROACH appendix (ISIS 304801-CS6) and the mipomersen ISIS 301012-CS5/CS7/CS12 safety tables are all out of scope — pursue these via ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, Europe PMC supplementary files and FDA/EMA review documents instead.

RECOMMENDATION. Take the four sequence/chemistry vocabulary records (results 1-4) and the Chan 2008 trial (result 5); exclude the imetelstat row by name and report the error to CTD; treat result 6 as optional methodological support. Do not re-search CTD for this endpoint — the curation simply is not there, and the capability control above makes that finding solid enough to cite as a negative in the Phase 2 submission.

coverage_log.notes:
Method note for the coverage log: the decisive query form is the documented assays-only POST (body {"assays":["<group>"]} with no chemids), which returns every chemical in ICE tested in that assay group — this is what allows a defensible "zero oligonucleotides in ICE's coagulation space" statement rather than a per-compound negative. Combined with the bulk-file scans, the search is exhaustive over ICE's whole inventory rather than sampled.

Negative-result statistics worth recording: 41/42 oligonucleotide name probes negative with a working positive control (warfarin, 2,342 records); 0 oligonucleotides in 2,831,021 cHTS rows; 0 oligonucleotides among 1,740 chemicals in "Regulation of Blood Coagulation" and 9,278 in "CardioTox - Endothelial Injury/Coagulation"; 0 oligonucleotides in nine in vivo/in vitro bulk datasets; 1 oligonucleotide in ADME Parameters. The only "phosphorothioate" matches across ICE are organophosphate pesticides (fenitrothion, malaoxon, phosalone, triazophos, isofenphos, phenthoate, chlorpyrifos, pirimiphos-methyl, methyl parathion, diazinon, azamethiphos, sulfotep, profenofos, isazofos, thiotepa, chlorethoxyfos, fenthion, chlorpyrifos-methyl, parathion, coumaphos, phosmet, tebupirimfos) — chemically unrelated to an oligonucleotide PS backbone and a false-positive trap for any keyword-driven harvest of this resource; they should be explicitly excluded if ICE or CompTox is ever re-queried by substructure.

NAMED ACQUISITION TARGETS - ALL ABSENT. "NCT03417245" = 0 hits (no ATLAS-A/B primary publication or safety appendix). "ATLAS-A" OR "ATLAS-B" returned 371 hits but the hyphen tokenises to "atlas" and every hit was beetle/blackfly taxonomic treatments; nothing relevant. "volanesorsen" = 0 (no APPROACH / ISIS 304801-CS6 supplementary appendix). "IONIS-FXIRx" OR "fesomersen" = 1, a narrative FXI-inhibitor review (record 20458008, World Journal of Pharmaceutical Research) with no primary data. Conclusion for the acquisition list: none of the five named targets is retrievable from Zenodo; pursue them via journal supplementary files, PMC, or the sponsor/regulatory route instead.

GAPS 3 AND 4. Only record 5878873 supplies printed sequences, and they are for DNA SELEX aptamers, not for any of the 38 clinically dosed compounds, so it does not move the 14-of-38 sequence count or the 11-of-38 position-level-chemistry count. Gap 4 is unserved: I found no record anywhere on Zenodo reporting % purity with method for a tested oligonucleotide.

coverage_log.notes:
COVERAGE AND METHOD. Searched the open REST API (https://datadryad.org/api/v2/search?q=...&per_page=100) rather than the web UI, per the resource-preference rule; 62 queries executed, every one returning a parsed result set. The API needs no auth for search and metadata. Note on interpreting counts: Dryad's search is fuzzy/OR-weighted across multi-token queries, so non-zero totals are often noise ("factor XI" returned 31 hits, led by prairie-lizard digestion and songbird plumage; "ATLAS-A/B" returned Mediterranean legume phylogeography). The informative signal is therefore the ZERO totals, which are reliable.

HARD NEGATIVES — all of these returned total=0, meaning the Dryad index contains no record mentioning them at all: volanesorsen, inotersen, mipomersen, olezarsen, donidalorsen, eplontersen, fitusiran, custirsen, pegnivacogin, defibrotide, gapmer, methoxyethyl, NCT03417245, "oligonucleotide coagulation", "antisense thrombocytopenia", "factor XI antisense", "oligonucleotide human plasma coagulation", "platelet oligonucleotide", prekallikrein, anti-Xa, thromboelastography, "aptamer anticoagulant", "CpG oligodeoxynucleotide", "hemostasis antisense", "bleeding antisense oligonucleotide", "clotting oligonucleotide", "fibrinogen oligonucleotide", "oligonucleotide whole blood", "oligonucleotide donors plasma", "antithrombin siRNA", "apolipoprotein antisense", "transthyretin antisense", "lipoprotein(a) antisense", "oligonucleotide purity HPLC". None of the named acquisition targets in gap 5 exist in Dryad.

GAP 1 (human in vitro/ex vivo coagulation with oligos): NOT CLOSED, and confirmed absent. Dryad does hold human coagulation datasets, but none involves oligonucleotide exposure, so they are off-scope rather than near-misses and I deliberately kept them out of the results list: doi:10.5061/dryad.3r2280ggj (coagulation abnormalities in dengue, systematic review/meta-analysis), doi:10.5061/dryad.612jm645d (basic coagulation parameters in COVID-19), doi:10.5061/dryad.pg4f4qrn3 (ICU COVID-19 coagulation profile, ROTEM), doi:10.5061/dryad.3ds63 (sepsis-induced coagulopathy criteria), doi:10.5061/dryad.gn5c8 (hemostatic dysfunction in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy), doi:10.5061/dryad.cjsxksn7r (blood biomarkers in COVID-19 prognosis). These could serve only as non-oligo reference ranges for aPTT/PT/platelets, not as evidence about any compound.

GAP 2 (human-to-animal bridge): NOT CLOSED. No Dryad deposit measures the same oligonucleotide construct in both a human system and an animal.

GAP 3 (exact sequence + per-position chemistry for clinically dosed oligos): essentially NOT CLOSED. Dryad's other antisense deposits are all preclinical neuroscience with no coagulation and no clinically dosed compound — doi:10.5061/dryad.1vhhmgr7k (atrophin-1/ATN1 ASO in humanized DRPLA mouse), doi:10.5061/dryad.6wwpzgn8j (mutant huntingtin intron-1 ASO in HttQ111/+ mice), doi:10.5061/dryad.3xsj3txw1 (SMN ASO redox in SMA mice). The two nusinersen deposits (doi:10.5061/dryad.n37q406, phase 1/2 later-onset SMA long-term results; doi:10.5061/dryad.1jwstqjs8, iSMAC respiratory trajectories) are human clinical data but report neuromuscular/respiratory outcomes, not coagulation, and carry no sequence or chemistry tables. Only AYX1 gives a clinically dosed compound whose chemistry is pinned down, and only because the abstract states it is an unprotected (unmodified) 23-bp duplex.

GAP 4 (purity and characterisation): PARTIALLY CLOSED for one compound, pending the download barrier. AYX1 Supplemental Tables 1-2 are genuine formulation stability/integrity data for the tested material. This is the single item worth pursuing from Dryad.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP. The AYX1 supplementary tables are CC0 and only a browser check away — retrieving doi:10.5061/dryad.dh250 from an environment that can clear the Anubis interstitial (or via the Dryad dataset ZIP in an ordinary browser) would settle (a) whether the rat clinical pathology panels in Supplemental Tables 3 and 8 include aPTT/PT/fibrinogen/platelet count, and (b) whether Supplemental protocol information prints the 23-bp decoy sequence. If yes to either, this yields one new animal coagulation record plus sequence, chemistry and stability characterisation for a human-dosed oligonucleotide. Outside that, Dryad should be treated as exhausted for this endpoint; do not re-run it.

acquisition_plan.summary:
Triage of ~80 visible records (the supplied list is TRUNCATED mid-record at Zenodo 5878873, so roughly 8 of the claimed 88 were not assessable — re-send the tail if it matters). 24 duplicate rows collapsed into 45 ranked entries. Ranking favours human in vitro/ex vivo assays and per-position chemistry on clinically dosed compounds; animal-only and expression-only records fall to the bottom regardless of how relevant their titles look.

THREE VERIFIED CORRECTIONS from direct checks of the primary records — all three would have corrupted the dataset if taken on trust:
1. PMID 9361909 (Henry 1997, "Inhibition of coagulation by a phosphorothioate oligonucleotide") is MISCLASSIFIED by the Semantic Scholar record as "human plasma clotting assays in vitro". I pulled the Europe PMC core record: it is cynomolgus monkey in vivo PLUS citrated blood from untreated MONKEYS in vitro. The MeSH "Humans" tag is the likely cause of the error. It does not close the human in vitro gap. Its real value is as the animal anchor of the ISIS 2302 same-construct triangle, plus a backbone contrast (PS vs phosphodiester vs 2'-propoxy, the latter two "much less inhibitory") and chromogenic negatives for FXa/FXIa/thrombin.
2. PMC8804562 (Haematologica) GPVI affinities are MICROMOLAR and compound-specific, not "KD ~0.2-1.5 mM" uniformly as the record states: 487660 = 0.2-1.5 uM, 104838 = 24 uM, 501861 = 26 uM. This inverts the naive story — 487660 has the HIGHEST GPVI affinity yet is the compound with no clinical platelet effect, so binding affinity must not be encoded as a monotonic predictor of the clinical phenotype. Confirmed 7 human donors, correlation r=0.85-0.97.
3. PMC10143489 (minipig) — the three triage records disagreed, with BioStudies calling the human arm UNVERIFIED and PubMed asserting a bridge matrix. I read it: Table 1 does give per-position chemistry for 7 constructs (length 14-22, PS load 0-21, so the PO variants are included), and Table 2 IS a 3-species table with a Human column for the same 7 constructs. BUT the human/NHP cells are CATEGORICAL literature-collated outcomes (activation / aggregation / no effect), not numeric human values. Acquire it for the chemistry table and a qualitative concordance map, not as human observations. Supplementary Table S1 is a juvenile-minipig sample overview only and need not be acquired.

OTHER TRAPS CARRIED FORWARD: the Southampton eprints file offered as an open ATLAS-A/B route is named Fitusiran_003_ATLAS_INH — a different trial (NCT03417102) — so use the registry artifacts instead; the BioStudies supplement for PMC12451317 (fitusiran assay interference) is the wrong file entirely, containing a search strategy about dental caries; and the Amsterdam UMC copy of APPROACH was text-verified to be main text only, so the NEJM appendix remains unclosed and should be chased through FDA/EMA review documents rather than more repository hunting.

HIGHEST-LEVERAGE SPEND: entries 1-5 are all open access and close human in vitro, human clinical-panel, dual purity, and per-position chemistry gaps at zero acquisition cost. The one paywalled item worth real document-delivery budget is entry 6 (Sheehan 1998 Blood + 2001 Biochemistry) — whether PS aPTT prolongation is saturable/allosteric or concentration-linear/polyanionic determines how the whole dataset extrapolates between assay formats and species. Entries 11-14 are the cheapest route to gap 3: sponsor protocols on ClinicalTrials.gov print position-level chemistry for inotersen, volanesorsen and olezarsen, and four CTD/MeSH systematic names give full sequences for four uniform-PS clinically dosed compounds.

ALREADY-IN-SOURCES FLAGS: no local manifest exists in the working directory, so this could not be verified mechanically.
